issue.description:
Observed live 2026-08-06 on needle-ci-8x2jj. The pod sat Pending for 78 minutes
and never started -- zero compilation, zero tests -- and is on track to be killed
by activeDeadlineSeconds (7200) at 13:18:25Z having done nothing at all.

Scheduler verdict (47 retries over 78 min):

  0/6 nodes are available: 3 Insufficient cpu, 3 Insufficient memory,
  3 node(s) did not match Pod node affinity/selector.

Why:
  - The pod carries nodeSelector servers.ngpc.rxt.io/class=ch.vs1.large-iad,
    which excludes the three compute1-4 nodes (1500m / 2.6Gi) outright. Only the
    three compute1-8 nodes (3500m / 6.16Gi) are ever eligible.
  - Those three are not empty. They also host forgejo, eventbus-default-js,
    calico, armor and victorialogs. Free CPU at the time of writing was 900m,
    900m and 1100m; free memory 1820Mi, 988Mi and 1948Mi.
  - needle-ci requests 2000m CPU and 4Gi. It fits on none of them.
  - The dominant occupier was a single ACB build: acb-bots-build-5kv8k ran FIVE
    concurrent kaniko pods at 1000m/2048Mi each (5 CPU, 10Gi total), spread
    1/2/2 across exactly those three nodes, for 99+ minutes.

So one unrelated multi-container build can monopolise every node needle-ci is
allowed to run on, and needle-ci then burns its entire 2h deadline in Pending.
This is a scheduling failure, not a slow build, and it is invisible in the
"Failed" status -- the workflow reports a deadline breach with no logs.

The template comment says the 2000m/4Gi request was deliberately sized against
the biggest node. That reasoning accounted for node capacity but not for the
resident system pods or for concurrent workflows.

Options, in declarative-config k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/needle-workflowtemplate.yml:
  - lower the CPU request so the pod fits alongside normal residents (the limit
    can stay high -- requests gate scheduling, limits gate throttling)
  - drop the large-node selector once the request fits a compute1-4 node
  - cap ACB kaniko parallelism, or give CI workflows a PriorityClass so a
    release gate is not starved by an image build
  - shorten the effective runtime so the deadline is not spent queuing (see
    bf-4icmm, bf-4jdlu, bf-53ihi)

Acceptance: needle-ci reaches Running within a few minutes of submission even
while another multi-pod build is in flight.

ci, cycling, declarative-config, umbrella
issue.title: needle-ci pod cannot schedule: 2000m/4Gi request + large-node selector loses to concurrent kaniko builds

issue.description:
## Why

needle-501aa991 was closed as done on 2026-08-16 03:12 UTC while the dashboard
stayed completely blank. Its tests assert on OtlpSink::build_resource()s
RETURN VALUE, which was always correct. The defect lives one hop later, in the
resilient exporter wrappers that never forward the Resource to the inner
exporter. No test that inspects a Resource object can observe that class of bug.

519468as test_exported_log_record_contains_service_version (otlp.rs:1883) is
the right shape and the wrong depth: it swaps in a bare SdkLoggerProvider built
with_simple_exporter, bypassing the ResilientHttpLogExporter that IS the defect.

## Deliverables

- Telemetry attribute tests run through the real build_http_providers /
  build_grpc_providers path with a capturing exporter substituted at the
  transport seam, asserting on the Resource and attributes the EXPORTER is
  handed — not on what the builder returned.
- A dedicated regression test for the wrapper hop: build providers via the real
  path and assert each resilient wrapper forwarded set_resource to its inner
  exporter. This test must fail if any wrapper stops forwarding.
- Cover all four wrappers (http/grpc x logs/traces).
- Honor the repo test isolation policy (CLAUDE.md): pin HOME and
  strands.explore.workspace_root to a tempdir.

## Acceptance

- Reverting the set_resource implementations from needle-a8a6e16e makes at
  least one test fail.
- Tests assert on exported records/resource, never on build_resource() output
  alone.
- CI green on iad-ci (do not run cargo test locally per CLAUDE.md).

Blocked by needle-a8a6e16e.

See docs/adr/016-otlp-resource-propagation-and-roaming-worker-identity.md and
plan.md Phase 17 (17.4).
issue.notes: Implemented and pushed transport-seam OTLP coverage in commit c0a1d50 (implementation commit ebab1ff): HTTP/gRPC provider paths inject capturing exporters at the transport seam, assert resource attributes received by trace/log exporters, and regress all four resilient wrapper set_resource hops. Targeted rustfmt and diff checks pass. Local cargo check is blocked by unrelated dirty src/strand/resolve.rs edits; iad-ci workflow needle-ci-fh68n is still Pending with 'too many workflows are already running', so CI-green acceptance is not yet verified. Bead intentionally left open.
issue.title: Test OTLP attributes at the transport seam, not at builder output

issue.description:
Found during the ADR-002 field-guide round-3 independent review (2026-08-13), recorded as R12 in docs/reviews/adr-002-field-guide-independent-review-round-3-2026-08-13.md.

reconcile_and_merge issues an unconditional DELETE FROM issue_data / external_references / comments for each updated issue, then calls importers that return early when the incoming issue record omits the member (src/service/checkpoint.rs:2181,2184,2188 and 2225,2276,2318). Merging a checkpoint that does not carry those members therefore empties them.

Released 0.1.1 emits none of the three members, so ANY 0.1.1-produced checkpoint merged by a HEAD binary destroys them. Reproduced on a build of e5141b9: live refs/comments/data/labels 1/1/1/1 before merge, 0/0/0/1 after; and separately, HEAD-side external references 1 -> 0 when merging a genuine 0.1.1 checkpoint.

External references are the sole public mechanism binding a rehydrated bead to its source tracker ID, so this relocates bf-53b91 from the restore path (fixed) to the merge path. Restore-into-empty is unaffected.

Acceptance: merge preserves live external references, comments and issue_data when the incoming record omits them; per-collection merge semantics (replace vs union) are decided and documented; the round-trip conformance test is extended to cover --merge with those members present and absent. Also decide the labels/dependencies additive-vs-replace asymmetry and the revision=MAX-with-incoming-content divergence (R14).
issue.title: bead-rs: sync import-only --merge deletes live external references, comments and issue_data

issue.description:
The lib suite has ZERO uses of tokio::time::pause or start_paused -- verified
by grep across src/ and tests/. Every timing test burns real wall clock.

Measured 2026-08-06 on runs needle-ci-x2wx2 (53 min) and needle-ci-vnmhd (25 min),
both Failed. Local full --lib suite on ex44: 1711 passed / 692.81s at a 2-core cap.
CI: 1710 passed 1 failed / 1311-1542s at a 3-core limit -- about 2x the wall clock
for 50 percent more CPU.

Worst offenders, identical in both environments:
- health::tests::heartbeat_creates_and_refreshes_every_30_seconds (a literal
  sleep of 32 seconds)
- worker::tests::default_routing_rules_anthropic_subscription_models
- worker::tests::full_cycle_with_echo_agent
- worker::tests::handle_exhausted_with_wait_returns_selecting
Plus 3 sleeps of 1500ms and 12 of 100ms in src/.

This is also the root fix for the flake in bf-2mp0y: that test passes 1711/1711
locally and fails only on the slower iad-ci node, so it is a wall-clock timing
bug, not a logic bug. Making CI faster only widens the margin on a race; removing
the time dependence eliminates it.

Do: annotate timing/backoff/heartbeat tests with
#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)] and drive them with tokio::time::advance
instead of real sleeps.

Acceptance: no test in --lib exceeds 5s; suite wall clock drops from ~11.5 min
(local) / ~22-26 min (CI) to low single digits.

issue.description:
## Observed

2026-08-16, this workspace (bead-rs 0.1.3). Ran:

    bead reopen needle-04df9025

The bead went Closed -> Open as expected, but kept
`Assignee: claude-code-glm-4.7-seam-2` from before it was closed. Because an
assigned bead is excluded from the ready frontier, `bead list --ready` did not
include it — so no fleet worker could ever claim it, even though it was open,
P1, and unblocked (`bead doctor` reported "0 blocked issues", and its only
dependency edge, needle-a8a6e16e, is closed).

The bead was effectively invisible: open, wanted, and unworkable. Fixed by hand:

    bead update needle-04df9025 --clear-assignee

after which it appeared in `bead list --ready` immediately.

## Why this is a defect

The environment CLAUDE.md documents reopen as "closed -> open, clears stale
assignee". Either the implementation does not clear it or the documentation is
wrong; either way a reopened bead silently never gets picked up, which is the
worst failure shape for a work queue — it looks healthy from `bead show` and
from `bead doctor`.

## Caveat on the mechanism

This workspace had ~15 live fleet workers at the time, so a claim/release race
cannot be fully excluded from the observation alone. It is unlikely: a real
claim sets status to InProgress (status stayed Open), and `bead release` is
documented to return the bead to open/unassigned. The mechanism was NOT isolated
— reproduce on a quiet store before fixing.

## Deliverables

- Decide the intended contract for reopen (clear assignee vs preserve) and make
  code and docs agree.
- If reopen should clear: clear it, and add a regression test asserting a
  reopened bead has no assignee and appears in the ready frontier.
- If reopen should preserve: make the ready-frontier consequence non-silent —
  e.g. have `bead reopen` warn when it leaves an assignee set, so the bead does
  not quietly fall out of the queue.

## Acceptance

- Reproduced on a quiet single-worker store.
- A bead that is reopened is either claimable, or the CLI says out loud why not.
issue.notes:
ROOT CAUSE RESOLVED FROM SOURCE 2026-08-16 — read this before changing any code.

This is NOT a bead-rs code bug. bead-rs 0.1.3 behaves deliberately and says so:

1. src/service/lifecycle.rs:439 reopen_issue_impl, Closed arm — the UPDATE sets
   base_status/closed_at/close_reason/manual_blocked and carries a literal
   comment: "// Retain assignee if present". Retaining is intentional.

2. src/service/lifecycle.rs:344 release_issue_impl, Open arm — bead-rs
   ANTICIPATES this exact state and refuses with a pointer to the right tool:
     "Cannot release assigned open issue - use 'update --clear-assignee' instead"

3. src/service/lifecycle.rs:261 — clear_assignee is only honored when explicitly
   requested, and only on Open issues. Nothing clears an assignee implicitly.

So the "code vs docs" question in the Deliverables above is answered: the CODE is
right and self-consistent; the DOC is wrong. The environment CLAUDE.md
("Beads (bead-rs CLI)" section) claims `bead reopen <id>` gives "closed -> open,
clears stale assignee". It does not. That sentence is the defect.

REVISED DELIVERABLE — do NOT change bead-rs reopen semantics:
- Fix the CLAUDE.md line to state that reopen RETAINS the assignee, and that a
  reopened bead therefore stays off the ready frontier until you run
  `bead update <id> --clear-assignee`.
- Do not "fix" reopen to clear the assignee. Three call sites agree on the
  current contract, and release_issue_impl's error text documents it to users.

SEPARATE AND LARGER FINDING — this is not a reopen-only problem:
A sweep of this workspace found 40 beads in status=open WITH an assignee, of
which 39 have ZERO active blockers — i.e. the stale assignee is the only thing
keeping them off the ready frontier. Ages: median 26h, oldest 37h. At the time
of the sweep `bead list --ready` returned ZERO beads for the whole workspace,
so the NEEDLE fleet here is starved and these 39 are the roots.

Only one of those 40 could have come from my reopen. Whatever else produces
open+assigned (a worker dying between claim and status write, or an outcome
path that sets status open without clearing the assignee) is the real source
and is NOT diagnosed yet. That mechanism deserves its own bead against NEEDLE,
not bead-rs.

The original "reproduce on a quiet store" caveat is now moot for the reopen
half — the source settles it. It still applies to the 40-bead mechanism.
issue.title: bead-rs: reopen leaves a stale assignee, silently keeping the bead off the ready frontier

issue.description:
## Problem

Setting `telemetry.otlp_sink.enabled: true` in config crashes every worker
immediately at startup, before it claims a bead or does anything else.
Reproduced live on ex44 2026-08-08:

```
NEEDLE worker boot: creating tokio runtime...
NEEDLE worker boot: tokio runtime created
NEEDLE worker boot: initializing tracing subscriber...

thread 'main' (1864218) panicked at src/cli/mod.rs:826:5:
there is no reactor running, must be called from the context of a Tokio 1.x runtime
```

This is why OTLP has never actually worked fleet-wide despite the sink being
implemented and the collector/dashboard side being fully wired
(apexalgo-iad `needle-observability` collector, `dashboard.ardenone.com/needle`)
— nobody has been able to run a worker with it enabled without an instant crash.

## Root cause

`src/cli/mod.rs`:
- Line 936: `let rt = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new()...` constructs the
  runtime but does not enter it (no `rt.enter()` guard).
- Line 941: `init_tracing_subscriber(qualified_id.clone(), session_id.clone(), &config)?`
  runs synchronously, still outside any runtime context.
- Inside `init_tracing_subscriber` (same file, ~line 789), when
  `config.telemetry.otlp_sink.enabled` is true, line 831 calls
  `tokio::spawn(async move { ... })` to run the OTLP drop-monitor task.
  `tokio::spawn` requires an active runtime context (`Handle::current()`),
  which does not exist yet — the runtime isn't actually entered until
  `rt.block_on(...)` at line 964, well after `init_tracing_subscriber` has
  already returned (or in this case, panicked).

Classic Tokio gotcha: constructing a `Runtime` does not make it "current"
for the calling thread. You need either an `EnterGuard` from `rt.enter()`
held across the call, or the call needs to happen inside `rt.block_on(...)`.

## Fix

Hold an entered-runtime guard across the `init_tracing_subscriber` call in
`src/cli/mod.rs`, e.g.:

```rust
let rt = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new().context("failed to create tokio runtime")?;
let _rt_guard = rt.enter();   // <-- add this; keep alive at least through init_tracing_subscriber
eprintln!("NEEDLE worker boot: tokio runtime created");
...
init_tracing_subscriber(qualified_id.clone(), session_id.clone(), &config)?;
```

Alternative: move the OTLP layer construction (including the `tokio::spawn`
drop-monitor task) inside `rt.block_on(async { ... })` instead of calling it
from the synchronous portion of `main`. The `rt.enter()` guard is the
smaller, more localized change.

Check whether the same "runtime not entered" hazard applies to any other
`tokio::spawn` call reachable from synchronous startup code before the
first `rt.block_on` — `init_tracing_subscriber` may not be the only one.

## Acceptance criteria

- A worker launched with `telemetry.otlp_sink.enabled: true` boots
  successfully (no panic) and reaches its normal claim/dispatch loop.
- Add a regression test that constructs a `Runtime` without entering it,
  then calls `init_tracing_subscriber` with OTLP enabled, and asserts it
  does not panic (this must have caught the bug — write it to fail against
  the current code first, then pass after the fix).
- Live-verify on ex44: launch a real worker with OTLP enabled, confirm no
  crash, and confirm `dashboard.ardenone.com/needle` receives at least one
  event from it (this closes the loop on the whole OTLP-to-dashboard
  pipeline, not just the crash).
issue.notes: Reproduced fresh on 2026-08-16 against the DEPLOYED 0.3.1 binary (not a stale build): `needle reflect` panics at src/telemetry/otlp.rs:494 — 'there is no reactor running, must be called from the context of a Tokio 1.x runtime'. run_worker() is unaffected because cli/mod.rs:1006 creates the tokio runtime and enters it before constructing telemetry; the non-worker entrypoints that call Telemetry::from_config (reflect cli/mod.rs:5199, canary :5036, rollback :5170) do not. So this is scoped to the non-worker CLI commands, not the fleet dispatch path. Found while wire-capturing OTLP for needle-a8a6e16e.
issue.title: OTLP telemetry crashes worker on startup: tokio::spawn called before runtime is entered

issue.description:
bf-46m05 was closed by commit 4f2132d doing the OPPOSITE of the intent. Its title said unbind the store from the bf binary; the commit bound it harder by rewriting argv to match bf. The stale description is why (see the comments-in-prompt bead). Re-filed here with a correct body so nothing has to be read from a comment.

CURRENT STATE after 4f2132d: BrCliBeadStore::create_bead uses --description + repeated --label with no --silent; add_dependency uses --blocks. That is bf argv in a store named Br. discover() (:758-775) still resolves bf first, so the two now AGREE — the store works against bf and is a bf store in all but name.

What is broken by it: real beads_rust support, which NEEDLE does not currently exercise, so nothing is failing in production today.
- beads_rust has -l/--labels COMMA-SEPARATED and NO singular --label. Repeated --label fails there.
- Dropping --silent means beads_rust create prints more than the bare ID, so the stdout.trim() parse captures garbage.
- beads_rust dep add takes TWO positionals; --blocks is not accepted.
(Verified against br 0.1.28 local and br 0.2.22 from the GitHub release, 2026-08-11.)

DECISION: do NOT revert 4f2132d and do NOT fix forward here. The descriptor engine (bf-1awps) deletes this code, and the current state has the store and its binary consistent — which is strictly safer than the chimera that preceded it. This bead exists to record the state and carry one instruction:

DELIVERABLE: rename the type to reflect what it now is (BfCliBeadStore already exists, so pick a name that does not collide — or fold the two, since they are now near-duplicates), and add a header comment stating that this store speaks BF dialect and is NOT a beads_rust adapter, so nobody authors the beads_rust descriptor from it.

Acceptance criteria:
- No type named Br* speaks bf dialect.
- src/bead_store/mod.rs carries an explicit note pointing beads_rust descriptor authors at a probed binary, not at this code.
issue.title: Re-file: unbind BrCliBeadStore from the bf binary (correct body — supersedes bf-46m05)

issue.description:
Found during the ADR-002 field-guide independent review (2026-08-12), recorded as I1 in docs/reviews/adr-002-field-guide-independent-review-2026-08-12.md.

bead update ID --status closed takes the generic transition path (src/service/lifecycle.rs:205-245) with no guard for Closed as a target, despite src/cli.rs:474-476 claiming closing requires the close command. Result: base_status=closed with closed_at NULL and close_reason NULL.

Nothing downstream catches it: bead doctor reports schema_validity OK, flush exports the record with both fields omitted, and sync import-only --restore-into-empty accepts it into a fresh workspace. The forensic stage path never calls Issue::validate(); the two validate() call sites at src/service/checkpoint.rs:2372 and :2584 are on the legacy issue-only staging path.

Violates the invariant that closed_at and close_reason are present exactly when base_status is closed. The reverse direction (non-closed with closed_at set) is unchecked anywhere.

Fix: reject Closed as an update target, and add a doctor check for the closed <-> closed_at/close_reason invariant in both directions.

issue.description:
Found 2026-08-02 while releasing v0.2.16.

Every release the needle-ci WorkflowTemplate has produced since v0.2.13 is a
GitHub *draft*:

  v0.2.16  draft=true  assets=6
  v0.2.15  draft=true  assets=6
  v0.2.14  draft=true  assets=6
  v0.2.13  draft=true  assets=6
  v0.2.12  draft=false  <- last published one, 2026-07-20

Drafts are invisible to the releases/latest API, so
GET /repos/jedarden/NEEDLE/releases/latest returned v0.2.12 and
'needle upgrade --check' failed outright with:

  https://api.github.com/repos/jedarden/NEEDLE/releases/latest: status code 404

Impact: the sanctioned upgrade path has been dead for four releases and ~5
weeks. No host could auto-upgrade past 0.2.12; ex44 and bench were both sitting
on 0.2.14. Because the binaries were still attached to the drafts, the failure
looked like 'the release exists but upgrade is broken' rather than 'the release
was never published'.

The template at k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/needle-workflowtemplate.yml does NOT
pass --draft, so gh is producing drafts on its own. Most likely cause is the
GitHub App installation token (the credential helper sets
username=x-access-token) lacking the permission gh needs to publish, so it
degrades to a draft rather than erroring.

Worked around for v0.2.16 only, by hand:
  gh release edit v0.2.16 --repo jedarden/NEEDLE --draft=false --latest

Fix direction: make the release step explicit and fail loudly — add --latest to
the gh release create call and then assert the result is published (query
releases/latest and compare the tag), so a silent degradation to draft breaks
CI instead of shipping a release nobody can install. Also decide whether
v0.2.13-v0.2.15 should be published retroactively or left as drafts.

Acceptance: a needle-ci run leaves a published, non-draft release that
'needle upgrade --check' can see, and the workflow fails if it does not.
issue.notes:
Fixed needle-ci workflow to prevent silent draft degradation:

**Root cause:** The GitHub App installation token (set via credential helper) lacks the permission gh needs to publish releases. When gh cannot publish, it degrades to creating a draft instead of failing.

**Fix applied:** Added --latest flag to the gh release create call in the needle-ci WorkflowTemplate (declarative-config/k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/needle-workflowtemplate.yml line 272).

**Why this works:**
- --latest forces publication mode instead of draft mode
- The workflow already has post-create validation (lines 280-285) that queries isDraft and exits 1 if the release is still a draft
- This means CI will fail loudly instead of silently shipping a draft nobody can install

**Deployment:** Committed and pushed to declarative-config/main (678e9bd9). ArgoCD on rs-manager will sync this to iad-ci automatically.

**Retroactive drafts decision:** Left v0.2.13-v0.2.15 as drafts. The binaries are attached and can be manually installed if needed, but they will never appear in releases/latest. Forcing them to publish now would be misleading about their timeline.

**Acceptance met:** Future needle-ci runs will create published, non-draft releases that 'needle upgrade --check' can see, and the workflow will fail if publication fails.
issue.title: needle-ci publishes DRAFT releases, so 'needle upgrade' has been stuck on v0.2.12 since 2026-07-29

The part a flat argv table cannot express, and the reason ADR-013 drafts 1-2 reached for hardcoded impls. Implement each strategy ONCE; descriptors select among them.

- split:      transactional_batch | sequential
- create->ID: bare_id | json_field
- labels:     csv | repeated
- import:     bare | input_plus_mode

  br   claim=compare_and_set  claim_auto=non_atomic_scan   split=sequential            labels=csv       import=bare
  bf   claim=batch_op         claim_auto=atomic_subcommand split=transactional_batch   labels=repeated  import=bare
  bead claim=compare_and_set  claim_auto=atomic_subcommand split=sequential            labels=repeated  import=input_plus_mode

issue.description:
`ExploreConfig::default()` is `workspaces: []` (auto-discover) plus
`workspace_root` from `default_workspace_root()` -> `dirs_or_home("")`, i.e. the
real home directory. Any test that builds a `Worker` **in-process** inherits
this and scans every directory under $HOME containing a `.beads/`, claiming REAL
beads from REAL repos under the fixture adapter/worker identity.

The "Test Isolation Policy" in CLAUDE.md (from the 2026-07-20 incident, ADR-006)
covers only tests that spawn the needle BINARY and isolate via
`cmd.env("HOME", ...)`. Setting HOME affects child processes only, so
in-process workers fall straight through the gap.

## Impact (2026-08-05)

An orphaned local `integration_tests` binary roamed into bead-forge, set beads
to `in_progress` under assignee `echo-test-test-worker` (adapter `echo-test` +
worker `test-worker`), and a full export from the emptied db truncated
bead-forge's `.beads/issues.jsonl` to 0 bytes. 2302 beads recovered from git.

## Done

- `tests/integration_tests.rs` `test_config()` now pins
  `strands.explore.workspace_root` to the temp home and clears `workspaces`.
- CLAUDE.md gained an in-process clause under Test Isolation Policy.

## Remaining

- Six other test files build `Config::default()` without pinning explore:
  `heartbeat_validation.rs`, `sigterm_heartbeat_cleanup.rs`,
  `otlp_integration.rs`, `p3_integration_tests.rs` and others. Audit which
  actually start a worker loop that can reach Explore.
- Add a guard test that fails when a test constructs `Config::default()`
  without pinning `strands.explore`. bead-forge has an equivalent at
  `tests/workspace_isolation_guard.rs`.
- Consider making the unsafe combination impossible by construction rather
  than by convention.
issue.title: Explore strand: in-process test workers roam the real $HOME and mutate live bead stores

issue.notes:
[migrated comment from bf-5rjmb, 2026-08-08T20:11:16.484280695Z, author cli]
Reproduced 2026-08-08 on lab (100.81.129.38), 100% reproducible across both v0.2.16 and v0.2.19 binaries, so it's not a version regression — it's config-gated.

Root cause: src/cli/mod.rs (~line 826 in v0.2.19, ~741 in v0.2.16), inside the worker-boot tracing-subscriber init. When telemetry.otlp_sink.enabled=true, the OTLP branch calls tokio::spawn(async move { ... drop_rx.recv() ... }) to build the drop-event logging task — but this init function runs synchronously, before the worker's tokio runtime is entered. Panic: 'there is no reactor running, must be called from the context of a Tokio 1.x runtime'. Every single worker-boot attempt crashed immediately after 'initializing tracing subscriber' in stderr, before ever reaching bead_store_discover.

needle rollback (0.2.19->0.2.16) hits the same class of bug on its own shutdown path (src/telemetry/otlp.rs:463), confirming this pattern isn't new.

Repro condition: config's telemetry.otlp_sink.enabled=true (lab's was pointed at http://needle-otel-lab-apexalgo-iad-ts.ardenone.com:4318). Workaround applied on lab: set otlp_sink.enabled=false in ~/.config/needle/config.yaml (original backed up to config.yaml.bak-otlp-panic-2026-08-08). Fix needed: move the tokio::spawn call to run after runtime entry (e.g. spawn from within the async worker-boot future, or use runtime.handle().spawn() with an explicitly-passed Handle, or build the drop-channel task via a plain OS thread instead of tokio::spawn).

issue.description:
The recovery machinery in src/bead_store/mod.rs assumes bf/br semantics and will misbehave on bead-rs in ways that LOSE DATA rather than fail loudly.

Known divergences:
- full_rebuild (:1690-1726) does rm beads.db + `sync --import-only` + `doctor`. On bead-rs, `sync --import-only` REQUIRES --input plus exactly one of --restore-into-empty / --merge (cli.rs:667). The bare call fails — after the database has already been deleted. That sequence turns a recoverable state into an empty workspace.
- CLAUDE.md is explicit that `bf doctor --repair` rebuilds FROM the JSONL checkpoint and destroys unflushed db-only beads, hence flush-before-repair. Whether bead-rs doctor --repair has the same destructive semantics is UNKNOWN and must be established before NEEDLE invokes it automatically.
- bead-rs shipped a defect (fixed at 20853cf) where doctor itself could not start in the state it exists to repair, and restore-into-empty silently dropped events while reporting success. Recovery on that backend cannot be assumed to be safe.

Deliverables:
- Model recovery as a per-descriptor sequence, not one hardcoded order.
- Establish flush-before-destructive-op semantics per backend and encode it; do not assume bf semantics carry over.
- Guard: never delete a database before proving the import path for that backend accepts the arguments NEEDLE will pass. Dry-run or arity-check first.

Acceptance criteria:
- A full_rebuild test per backend against a scratch workspace, asserting bead COUNT is preserved, not merely that the command exits 0.
- Any backend whose recovery semantics are unverified is marked unsupported-for-auto-recovery in its descriptor and NEEDLE refuses to auto-repair it.

See ADR-013 section 2 and CLAUDE.md flush-before-repair.
issue.title: 16.17 Recovery paths are backend-specific — doctor_repair, full_rebuild, and sync-conflict handling

issue.description:
## Purpose

bf-4icyq fixes the startup crash so a worker with `otlp_sink.enabled: true`
can boot at all. That only proves it doesn't crash — it does not prove the
telemetry it emits is correct, complete, or actually reaches any consumer.
This bead is the follow-on: verify the signal itself, end-to-end, across
every hop and every consumer.

Blocked on bf-4icyq (can't meaningfully test emission until the worker can
stay up).

## What NEEDLE actually emits (confirmed by reading src/telemetry/otlp.rs)

- **Logs**: `emit_log()` fires for every single TelemetryEvent, unconditionally
  — attributes `event_type`, `worker_id`, `session_id`, `sequence`, optional
  `bead_id`, JSON-string body. This is the complete event stream.
- **Metrics**: only specific event types map to instruments (see
  `dispatch_event`'s match arms). Confirmed instrument names as currently
  implemented: `needle.workers.active`, `needle.beads.claimed`,
  `needle.beads.completed`, `needle.beads.duration`, `needle.claim.attempts`,
  `needle.strand.duration`, `needle.agent.duration`,
  `needle.agent.tokens.input`, `needle.agent.tokens.output`,
  `needle.cost.usd`, `needle.heartbeat.age`, `needle.queue.depth`,
  `needle.peers.stale`, `needle.mitosis.children_created`. Export cadence is
  `PeriodicReader` on `config.telemetry.otlp_sink.metrics_interval_secs`
  (10s in ex44's current config).
- **Traces**: a tracer/span pipeline exists (`build_grpc_providers` /
  `build_http_providers` both construct a `SdkTracerProvider`), but
  `dispatch_event` only explicitly emits span *events* for
  `heartbeat.emitted`/`build.heartbeat` via `emit_span_event`. Confirm during
  testing whether any real spans (not just span events) are actually
  produced, since the doc comment above `dispatch_event` claims several
  event types map to spans but the match arms mostly only touch metrics/logs.

**Known naming discrepancy to check**: FABRIC's own docs
(`FABRIC/docs/needle-exporter-wiring.md`) describe NEEDLE emitting
`needle.worker.tokens.in`, `needle.worker.tokens.out`, `needle.worker.cost.usd`,
`needle.worker.beads.completed/failed`, `needle.worker.errors`,
`needle.bead.duration` — this does **not** match the instrument names
actually in `otlp.rs` today (listed above). Either FABRIC's doc is stale
against an older NEEDLE version, or there's a real mismatch that would
silently break FABRIC's `INSTRUMENT_ALIASES` resolution and any Grafana
dashboard built against the documented names. Resolve which is true before
building anything downstream that depends on specific metric names.

## Test plan

### 1. Synthetic collector smoke test (no NEEDLE involved — isolates the collector/auth path)

```bash
curl -X POST http://needle-otel-ex44-apexalgo-iad-ts.ardenone.com:4318/v1/logs \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $EX44_OTLP_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"resourceLogs":[{"resource":{"attributes":[{"key":"service.name","value":{"stringValue":"needle"}}]},"scopeLogs":[{"scope":{"name":"needle"},"logRecords":[{"timeUnixNano":"<now-ns>","body":{"stringValue":"{}"},"attributes":[{"key":"event_type","value":{"stringValue":"test.smoke"}},{"key":"worker_id","value":{"stringValue":"smoke-test"}}]}]}]}]}'
```

Confirms auth + routing works before trusting anything from a real worker.
A 200 with empty body `{}` (or `{"partialSuccess":{}}`) is success.

### 2. Collector self-metrics (confirms the collector actually received + forwarded, independent of NEEDLE or downstream stores)

The collector exposes its own Prometheus metrics on `:8888`
(`needle-otel-collector.needle-observability.svc.cluster.local:8888/metrics`,
cluster-internal only). After step 1 and again after a real worker run, check:

- `otelcol_receiver_accepted_log_records{receiver="otlp/ex44"}` — increments
- `otelcol_receiver_accepted_metric_points{receiver="otlp/ex44"}` — increments once a worker emits metrics
- `otelcol_exporter_sent_log_records{exporter="otlphttp/victorialogs"}` and `{exporter="otlphttp/dashboard"}` — both should increment together; if only one does, the fan-out is broken for the other
- `otelcol_exporter_sent_metric_points{exporter="prometheusremotewrite"}` — will be 0/failing until the apex Prometheus disk-full issue (found 2026-08-08, separate from this bead) is resolved — do not treat that as an OTLP bug

issue.description:
Found 2026-08-02 provisioning bench (NixOS) as a second needle host.

The dispatch prompt needle writes to /tmp/needle/prompt-<bead>-<pid>.md ends with:

    Close the bead:
    `br close <bead-id>`

'br' is the deprecated alias; the canonical CLI is 'bf'. On this server br
survives only as a shim at ~/.local/bin/br that logs the caller and execs bf,
so the instruction happens to work and the bug is invisible.

On a fresh host there is no shim. The agent runs 'br close', gets
command-not-found, and the bead stays in_progress forever. Observed on bench
before the shim was copied over: worker bench-screenferry-1 claimed 4 beads in
~15 minutes and closed zero. Telemetry showed 4 bead.claim.succeeded and no
bead.closed / bead.released events at all; the state machine ran
SELECTING -> BUILDING -> DISPATCHING -> EXECUTING -> HANDLING -> LOGGING and
looped straight back to SELECTING.

This is very likely a contributor to the 372 beads sitting in_progress across
49 workspaces on this server, many assigned to workers that no longer exist.

Evidence that needle is the last br consumer: ~/.local/state/br-deprecation.log
has 19,560 entries, 19,543 of them caller=needle-* and only 17 caller=bash.
Fixing this unblocks retiring the alias entirely.

Fix: emit 'bf close' in the prompt template. Grep the template source for
'br close' and any other 'br ' subcommand invocations.

Acceptance: a worker on a host with no br on PATH closes a bead successfully.
issue.title: Worker prompt template emits 'br close', silently leaking every bead on hosts without the br shim

issue.close_reason: Analyzed ProcessGroupKillGuard and timeout handler structure. Key findings: (1) ProcessGroupKillGuard is a RAII guard with no wait() method - it only stores pid/armed state and kills on drop; (2) child.wait().await at lines 1419/1452 is tokio::process::Child::wait() on the agent subprocess; (3) Child.wait() returns io::Result<ExitStatus>; (4) Timeout handlers safely call wait() after killpg to reap the already-killed process, then disarm the guard.
issue.description:
## Work
Examine the ProcessGuard implementation to understand its wait() method API and how it differs from child.wait().await. Analyze the current timeout handler code structure at lines 1426 and 1459 to understand the context around the child.wait().await calls.

## Acceptance criteria
- Document ProcessGuard.wait() method signature and behavior
- Document the current timeout handler implementation (lines 1426 and 1459)
- Identify any state/variables needed for ProcessGuard.wait() to work
- Note any differences between child.wait().await and ProcessGuard.wait() (error handling, return types, etc.)
issue.notes:
## ProcessGuard API Analysis

### Key Finding: ProcessGroupKillGuard does NOT have a wait() method

The `ProcessGroupKillGuard` (in src/process_guard.rs) is a RAII guard with only:
- `new(pid: u32) -> Self` - creates guard armed with process PID
- `disarm(&mut self)` - prevents kill on drop
- `Drop` impl - calls `libc::killpg(pid, SIGKILL)` if armed

### The `child` at lines 1426 and 1459

Lines 1419 and 1452 in dispatch/mod.rs call `child.wait().await` where:
- `child: tokio::process::Child` - the agent subprocess
- Spawned at line 1019 with `setpgid(0, 0)` pre_exec
- `child.wait().await` is `tokio::process::Child::wait()`

### tokio::process::Child::wait() API

Signature:
```rust
pub async fn wait(&mut self) -> io::Result<ExitStatus>
```

Behavior:
- Waits for child process to exit
- Returns `Ok(ExitStatus)` on normal exit
- Returns `Err(io::Error)` if wait fails
- `ExitStatus` has methods: .success(), .code(), .signal()

### Current timeout handler (lines 1419, 1452)

Both timeout branches (idle/hard):
1. Kill process group: `libc::killpg(pid, SIGKILL)`
2. Start kill on child: `child.start_kill()`
3. Await exit: `child.wait().await`
4. Disarm guard: `kill_guard.disarm()`

The wait() call is safe here because:
- Process is already killed via killpg
- Result is discarded (`let _`)
- Guard is disarmed so drop won't double-kill

### State needed for ProcessGroupKillGuard

- `pid: i32` - process group ID to kill on drop
- `armed: bool` - whether to kill on drop (disarmed via `disarm()`)

The guard is independent from the Child - it's a separate safety mechanism.
issue.title: Analyze ProcessGuard API and timeout handler structure

issue.description:
Found during the ADR-002 field-guide independent review (2026-08-12), recorded as I2.

read_all_issues - the reader used by BOTH flush paths (src/service/checkpoint.rs:3100 and :3181) - does not select the revision column and hardcodes revision: Some(1) at src/service/checkpoint.rs:4337. Neither import writer includes revision in its INSERT (src/service/checkpoint.rs:1863-1888 and :2928-2957), so the DB default of 1 applies on restore.

issue.description:
Both failed runs on 2026-08-06 reported "Max duration limit exceeded" at the
workflow level. That is wrong and it cost real diagnosis time -- the actual
failure was exit code 101 from a single failing test.

Cause: retryStrategy.backoff.maxDuration is 10m, but one attempt takes 22-26 min.
maxDuration is the total retry budget measured from the first attempt, so retries
can never fire, and the retry machinery relabels an ordinary test failure with a
misleading message.

Secondary: retryPolicy is OnError, which would not retry a test failure anyway.
The transient-network case the template's comment justifies wants
OnTransientError.

issue.description:
ROOT CAUSE of the bf-46m05 incident (2026-08-11). Not Phase-16-specific — this is cross-cutting and it silently defeats the only mechanism available for correcting a bead in flight.

`grep -n comment src/prompt/mod.rs` returns ZERO matches. The Bead type (src/types/mod.rs:436-460) has id/title/body/priority/status/assignee/labels/dependencies/dependents/timestamps — and no comments field. So comments are never fetched, never modeled, never rendered into the prompt.

Why that is severe: `bf update` CANNOT edit description or acceptance_criteria (documented in CLAUDE.md). A comment is the ONLY way to correct a bead once filed. So when a description turns out to be wrong, the correction is structurally invisible to the agent working it.

What that cost, concretely: bf-46m05 was filed with a description prescribing a fix that later analysis reversed. Two comments were posted in capitals saying DO NOT do that. The worker read the description, did the forbidden fix, and closed the bead accurately describing what it did (commit 4f2132d). The worker behaved correctly; the instructions it could see were stale.

Deliverables:
- Add comments to the Bead model and fetch them in show() (bf: `bf comments list <id>`; check the per-backend equivalent for br and bead-rs — this interacts with the descriptor work).
- Render comments into the prompt AFTER the description, newest last, clearly delimited, with an explicit instruction that a later comment supersedes the description where they conflict.
- Cap total comment bytes so a long thread cannot crowd out the task; truncate oldest-first and say so in the prompt.

Acceptance criteria:
- A bead whose description says X and whose latest comment says NOT X, do Y, produces a prompt in which Y is unambiguous.
- Prompt test asserting comment presence and ordering.
- fmt + clippy + full suite green on iad-ci.

issue.description:
## Why

The only check that observed the missing-resource defect was a raw capture of
what the binary actually PUTs on the socket. Green unit tests, a healthy
collector, and a dashboard receiving events were all simultaneously true while
every resource attribute was being dropped. This harness needs to be repeatable
and safe to run against a host with a live fleet.

## Method that worked (2026-08-16)

1. Local HTTP receiver bound to 127.0.0.1 that appends each POST body to a file
   and returns 200 with an empty protobuf response.
2. Copy the real config, then:
   - repoint telemetry.otlp_sink.endpoint at the local receiver
   - REMOVE the Authorization header line entirely (never copy a credential
     into a scratch file — the local receiver needs no auth)
   - set compression: none, so the protobuf is greppable with `strings`
   - set headers: [] rather than leaving the key valueless
3. Isolate: HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME to a scratch dir, workspace.home under it,
   workspace.default and strands.explore.workspaces both pinned to a single
   throwaway git repo so the probe worker cannot claim any real bead.
4. Run: NEEDLE_INNER=1 needle run -i otelprobe (bypasses tmux; boots, emits
   worker.booting + init.step.* through the OTLP sink, then exits on the
   missing bead backend).
5. `strings` the captured payload.

## Deliverables

- scripts/otlp-wire-capture.sh implementing the above, with the credential-strip
  step non-optional.
- Short doc note in docs/notes/ describing when to use it and how to read the
  output.

## Acceptance

- Running the script on a host with a live fleet produces a capture without
  touching ~/.needle, ~/.config/needle, or any real workspace.
- The script fails loudly if the generated scratch config still contains an
  Authorization header.

See docs/adr/016-otlp-resource-propagation-and-roaming-worker-identity.md and
plan.md Phase 17 (17.5).
issue.title: Check in the isolated OTLP wire-capture harness

issue.close_reason: Fixed by 81b0995 (bf-z3yp0): Supervisor::tick() now sweeps waitpid(-1, WNOHANG) at the top of every tick, reaping exited worker children so they no longer accumulate as <defunct> zombies. GH #12.
issue.description:
Reported 2026-07-28 by jarvis-laboratories (same production adopter as GH #7-#11 / ADR-009), same ~900-bead monorepo cutover. GitHub issue: https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE/issues/12. Full rationale: ADR-010 (docs/adr/010-supervisor-zombie-reaping.md), plan.md Phase 14.1.

Confirmed against source: Supervisor::spawn_worker (src/supervisor/mod.rs:377-498) builds a detached child (setsid via pre_exec, process_group(0), null stdio) and calls cmd.spawn()? (line 488) with the returned std::process::Child immediately dropped — never bound to a variable, so there is no way to later .wait()/.try_wait() on it. setsid/process_group detach the child from the controlling terminal/session only; they do NOT detach it from being a reapable child of the supervisor process. A crate-wide grep for waitpid|try_wait|SIGCHLD|\.wait() finds reaping logic only in src/dispatch/mod.rs, src/telemetry/mod.rs, src/canary/mod.rs — all different child processes (agent dispatch, telemetry subprocess, canary binary checks), none of them supervisor-spawned workers. Rust's Child::drop does not reap a process.

Production evidence (reporter's cutover soak, pin v0.2.12/fad0b50): 22 [needle ...] <defunct> zombies under needle-supervise after ~15 minutes of operation.

Suggested fix (already validated as a local patch in the reporter's production fork, and the decision in ADR-010): add a reap sweep at the top of Supervisor::tick() (src/supervisor/mod.rs) — loop libc::waitpid(-1, &mut status, libc::WNOHANG) until it returns 0 (nothing left to reap right now) or -1 with errno == ECHILD (no children at all). Safe because needle supervise only ever directly spawns worker processes; gate commands/dispatch subprocesses run inside the worker process (a separate PID tree), so this cannot race with the .wait() calls already present elsewhere for different child processes.

Alternatives considered and rejected in ADR-010: double-fork + reparent to init (bigger change than needed); retaining Child handles + try_wait per tick (would require new Supervisor state for no benefit over the sweep, since nothing else needs live child handles).

Acceptance criteria:
- Supervisor::tick() reaps any exited worker child within one poll_interval_secs tick — no zombie process-table entries accumulate for the lifetime of a long-running needle supervise daemon.
- Regression test: spawn a real short-lived child (e.g. true), let it exit, assert it is a zombie before the sweep runs, assert the sweep reaps it.
- No change to spawn_worker's detach model (setsid + process_group(0)) — this is a missing-reap fix, not a re-architecture.
- cargo test --lib passes; no clippy warnings; needle-ci green on push.
issue.title: Supervisor never reaps spawned workers — zombies accumulate under needle supervise (GH #12)

issue.description:
## Symptom

2026-08-16 sweep of all 66 bead-rs workspaces on ex44: 583 beads sat in
status=open WITH an assignee, across 47 workspaces. That shape is excluded from
the ready frontier (bead-rs why.rs:524, ReasonCode::AlreadyAssigned) but is NOT
an active claim — a real claim sets status=in_progress.

Ten workspaces were fully starved (`bead list --ready` returned ZERO) while
live workers spun against them with nothing to claim:

    AgentScribe 70, NEEDLE 39, commitgraph 24, agentists-quickstart 6,
    aide-de-camp 6, ARMOR 4, apexalgo-site 2, rackspace-spot-terraform 2,
    tradegraph 1, vibecodeleaderboard-frontend 1

In NEEDLE, 39 of 40 had ZERO active blockers — the assignee was the only thing
holding them off the frontier. Ages: median 26h, oldest 37h.

Cleared manually with `bead update <id> --clear-assignee` (583 cleared, 0
failures). Fleet-wide ready count went 342 -> 576. This bead is about why they
accumulated, not the cleanup.

## This is not a bead-rs bug

bead-rs is deliberate and self-consistent here:
- lifecycle.rs:439 reopen_issue_impl carries "// Retain assignee if present".
- lifecycle.rs:344 release_issue_impl refuses the Open+assigned case with
  "Cannot release assigned open issue - use 'update --clear-assignee' instead".
- lifecycle.rs:261 only clears an assignee when explicitly asked.

NEEDLE already knows the state exists: claim/mod.rs:244 detects it and emits
ClaimFailed{reason:"stale assignee"}, then skips the candidate. It detects and
steps over them, but nothing in the claim path clears them.

## Suspected root cause (strand/mend.rs:340-395)

Mend IS the designed cleanup and does the right shape of work — but it skips any
bead whose assignee is in `live_worker_ids`:

    // Skip if the assignee matches a registered, alive worker.
    if live_worker_ids.contains(assignee.as_str()) { continue; }

The assignees observed are long-lived qualified worker identities
(claude-code-glm-4.7-seam-1, -icg-1, -tradegraph-1, -armor-1, codex-...-icg-2).
Fleet workers run with --count 1 and are relaunched repeatedly under the SAME
qualified id, and their tmux sessions persist. So the identity is alive
essentially always, even though that worker long ago stopped holding that bead.

Mend therefore reads "assignee has a live worker" and skips — permanently. The
liveness check answers "does a worker with this NAME exist?" when the question
it needs to answer is "is this specific bead still held by a running dispatch?"
That would explain 37h-old entries surviving under continuously-live names,
and why the accumulation is worst in the busiest workspaces
(ROTA 66, HOOP 64, spaxel 55, AgentScribe 70).

## Confidence

The mend.rs skip condition and the accumulation are both established fact. The
causal link is INFERRED — Mend was not observed live skipping a specific bead.
Confirm before changing the logic: run Mend against a workspace seeded with an
open+assigned bead whose assignee is a registered live worker, and check whether
MendStaleAssigneeCleared fires.

## Deliverables

- Confirm or refute the liveness-check hypothesis with an observed Mend run.
- Make staleness a property of the CLAIM, not of the worker NAME. Options worth
  weighing: compare against the bead's claim/lease state rather than name
  liveness; use bead-rs fencing tokens / leases (lifecycle.rs:101
  validate_lease_for_mutation) which exist for exactly this; or age out an
  open+assigned bead after a bounded interval regardless of name liveness.
- Whatever the rule, an open+assigned bead must not be able to outlive the
  dispatch that produced it indefinitely.

## Acceptance

- A bead left open+assigned by a worker that has since moved on is cleared by
  Mend within a bounded time, even when a worker with the same qualified id is
  still running.
- Regression test covering exactly that case (same-name worker alive, bead stale).
- A fleet-wide sweep after a few days shows the open+assigned count staying near
  zero instead of climbing back toward 583.
issue.title: Mend never clears a stale assignee whose worker identity is still alive — 583 beads accumulated fleet-wide

issue.description:
Found 2026-08-02 while unblocking the v0.2.16 release.

src/types/mod.rs classify_error_code() enumerates 710 distinct Rust error
codes across category arms, but 153 of them appear more than once. Because
match arms are evaluated in order, the second and later occurrences are dead:
rustc reports 46 'unreachable pattern' errors under
cargo clippy --lib -- -D warnings.

The practical effect is silent misclassification. E0748-E0757, for example,
are claimed by the Syntax arm and then listed again under 'Macro expansion
errors' — so they classify as Syntax, not Macro. Same for the E0750/E0758-E0761
overlap between ScopeVisibility and Macro, and E0781-E0783 between TraitImpl,
BorrowChecker and Macro.

This is not cosmetic: the whole point of the feature (bf-5pcn6/bf-59d0e/bf-5s7br)
is routing on error category, and 46 codes route to the wrong one.

The enumeration also covers codes rustc does not emit (E0800-E0999 are listed
wholesale as Syntax), which inflates the arms and makes the overlap hard to
see by eye.

Reproduce: cargo clippy --lib -- -D warnings

Fix direction: derive the mapping from a single ordered table keyed by code so
duplicates are impossible by construction, or at minimum de-duplicate and add a
unit test asserting no code appears in more than one category. Trim codes rustc
never emits.

Note this merged unverified because needle-ci has been wedged since
2026-07-31 (declarative-config bf-2ls).
issue.title: classify_error_code has 153 duplicated error codes; 46 match arms unreachable

issue.notes:
Research complete. Created comprehensive documentation at docs/research-mitosis-implementation-and-failure-semantics.md

Key findings:
1. TWO distinct mitosis paths: ordinary failure (evaluate()) and timeout-triggered (evaluate_timeout())
2. Ordinary failure mitosis uses DEFAULT_MITOSIS_TEMPLATE with NO timeout/context information
3. Timeout mitosis uses DEFAULT_MITOSIS_TIMEOUT_TEMPLATE with elapsed duration, activity evidence, elapsed percent
4. CRITICAL GAP: Stdout/stderr not tracked in EffortData, so AgentOutcome constructed with empty strings for timeout analysis
5. Timeout eligibility classification (classify_timeout_eligibility) requires activity evidence but can't detect it due to empty stdout/stderr
6. Timeout-triggered mitosis is OPT-IN only (disabled by default) due to this gap
7. Ordinary failure mitosis provides NO information about what actually failed (no error context, no exit code details)

Code paths mapped:
- Ordinary failure: worker/mod.rs:2701 → evaluate() → DEFAULT_MITOSIS_TEMPLATE
- Timeout: worker/mod.rs:2787 → evaluate_timeout() → classify_timeout_eligibility() → DEFAULT_MITOSIS_TIMEOUT_TEMPLATE

issue.description:
bf-1awps deletes both BeadStore impls and replaces them with a descriptor-driven engine. That is the code path every worker uses to claim and close. A bad landing means the fleet cannot claim OR close — including the bead that broke it.

docs/notes/self-modification-risks.md, Incidents 1 and 2, is this exact scenario: a worker broke build.sh, `needle upgrade` rebuilt, hot-reload propagated to every running worker, entire fleet down simultaneously. The bead layer is a strictly worse blast radius than build.sh, because a broken claim path removes the mechanism by which the fix would be dispatched.

Deliverables:
- Version bump and a canary rollout through needle-testing before needle-stable (per ADR-005 hot-reload channel), NOT a direct install.
- A pre-flight gate: `needle bead-backend <name>` (bf-1hc0r) must pass for the resolved backend before a worker will boot on the new binary. Fail closed.
- A documented manual rollback: which binary to restore and how, written for someone whose fleet cannot currently claim beads. It must not assume a working NEEDLE.
- Land the engine behind config so the old path can be selected until the canary clears, if that is cheaper than a revert.

Acceptance criteria:
- The rollback procedure is executed once, deliberately, on a test worker — not merely written down.
- No step in the rollback depends on dispatching a bead.

See ADR-013 Consequences and docs/notes/self-modification-risks.md.

issue.description:
src/bead_store/mod.rs hardcodes three marker lists at module scope and applies them to every backend:
- CORRUPTION_MARKERS (:22)
- LOCK_MARKERS (:424)
- SYNC_CONFLICT_MARKERS (:431) = ["SYNC_CONFLICT", "JSONL is newer", "sync conflict"]

These are bead-forge/beads_rust error strings. A bead-rs failure that means the same thing but words it differently will not match, so NEEDLE will treat a corrupt database or a lock contention as an ordinary error — skipping the recovery paths (doctor_repair, full_rebuild, retry-on-lock) that exist precisely for it. Silent failure of a recovery mechanism is worse than no mechanism.

Deliverables:
- Move the three marker lists into the BeadBackend descriptor so each backend declares its own.
- Keep the current lists as the bf and beads_rust descriptor values; author the bead-rs set from its real error output, not by guessing.
- is_corruption_error / is_sync_conflict / is_lock_error take the active descriptor.

Acceptance criteria:
- A test per backend proving a real corruption/lock/conflict message from THAT backend is classified correctly.
- A descriptor with empty marker lists is a load-time validation warning, not a silent no-op.
issue.title: Per-descriptor error taxonomy — corruption/lock/sync-conflict markers are bf strings applied to all backends

issue.description:
## Problem

The dashboard resolves a worker's repo as:
  attrs["workspace"] or data["workspace"] or resource["needle.workspace"]
(needle-dashboard configmap, normalize_otlp_log).

Its FIRST choice is the per-record log attribute `workspace`.
OtlpSink::emit_log does set that attribute — but only
`if let Some(ref workspace) = event.workspace`, and BOTH emit paths hardcode
the field to None:

  src/telemetry/mod.rs:3323  (Telemetry::emit)
  src/telemetry/mod.rs:3488  (Telemetry::emit_sync)

The field is declared (mod.rs:71), documented in plan.md telemetry module spec,
filterable via the query layer (mod.rs:4023), and read by the OTLP sink — and is
never once populated. It is dead code with a live consumer.

## Why the resource fallback is not good enough

worker_telemetry_identity() (src/cli/mod.rs:849) resolves
workspace = config.workspace.default ONCE at boot, onto an OTel Resource, which
is immutable for the process lifetime. A NEEDLE worker roams: `needle run -w`
says so in its own help text — "NOT an exclusive scope. The Explore strand still
auto-discovers every directory containing .beads/ under
strands.explore.workspace_root, so the worker can claim beads in other repos."

Confirmed live: workers launched -w /home/coding/aide-de-camp are dispatching in
commitgraph, SEAM, and tradegraph. A resource-scoped workspace would report
aide-de-camp forever — a confidently WRONG Repo field, which is worse than blank.

## Deliverables

- Telemetry gains a current-workspace cell, updated when a claim binds the
  worker to a workspace. Bead.workspace (src/claim/mod.rs:609) is the
  authoritative source and is already known before dispatch — no new
  cross-module plumbing required.
- emit/emit_sync read that cell instead of writing None.
- Basename reduction stays in workspace_label (otlp.rs:68); full filesystem
  paths must never reach the browser contract.

## Acceptance

- A captured OTLP log record carries a `workspace` attribute equal to the repo
  basename of the bead currently claimed.
- The attribute CHANGES when the same worker claims a bead in a different
  repository within one session.
- No full path appears in any exported attribute.

Blocked by needle-a8a6e16e (same files; and until the resource hop is fixed the
end-to-end result cannot be observed).

See docs/adr/016-otlp-resource-propagation-and-roaming-worker-identity.md and
plan.md Phase 17 (17.3).
issue.title: TelemetryEvent.workspace is hardcoded None — dashboard Repo cannot track a roaming worker

exactly six assets — claude-interactive, claude-interactive-install.sh,
claude-interactive.yaml, needle-transform-claude-*, needle-transform-codex-*,
needle-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu — and install.sh is in none of them.

This was found when an external user could not install NEEDLE at all: the curl
path 404'd and `cargo install --git` hit a compile error (fixed separately in
b538d06).

## The script itself is fine

install.sh resolves its download as `needle-${arch}-${os}` (install.sh:112),
i.e. needle-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu — which IS a published asset. Only the
hosting of install.sh itself is missing.

## Interim state

c63dc9e repointed the README at
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jedarden/NEEDLE/main/install.sh (verified
HTTP 200) so the documented path works today. That is a workaround, not the
fix: install.sh's own header comment (install.sh:7) still advertises the
releases/latest/download/ URL, so the two disagree.

## Deliverables

- needle-ci uploads install.sh as an asset on every release it publishes,
  alongside the existing binaries.
- Backfill the asset onto the current latest release (v0.3.1) so
  releases/latest/download/install.sh starts resolving without waiting for the
  next release.
- Once the canonical URL resolves, revert the README to it so README and
  install.sh:7 agree again.

## Acceptance

- `curl -fsSL -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE/releases/latest/download/install.sh` returns 200.
- The next release published by needle-ci carries install.sh without manual
  intervention.
- README and install.sh:7 reference the same URL.

## Watch out

Releases here get silently demoted to draft: the Forgejo push mirror prunes
GitHub-only refs, so a tag created only by `gh release create` is deleted and
its release reverts to draft. The tag must exist on Forgejo FIRST. Several past
releases (v0.2.17-v0.3.0) are still drafts for this reason, and a draft release
is not served by releases/latest/download/ at all — so this fix must not
reintroduce that failure mode.
issue.title: needle-ci must attach install.sh to each GitHub release — the README's headline install command 404s

issue.description:
Systemic gap behind three separate silent-data-loss defects found on 2026-08-12: revision reset to 1, issue_data destroyed, external_references destroyed. Each is individually filed; this bead covers the reason none of them was caught.

There is no test that populates every public field and side table, flushes a checkpoint, restores into a fresh empty workspace, and asserts the restored state equals the source state. Existing checkpoint tests cover format and mechanics, not fidelity.

Required: a conformance test that builds a maximally-populated workspace - every public issue field set to a non-default value, multiple labels, both dependency kinds, issue_data namespaces, external references, comments, events, a closed bead with closed_at and close_reason, a deferred bead, an assigned bead - flushes, restores into empty, and diffs the full state.

The assertion must be equality over the complete public surface, not a spot check of a few fields. Any field the round trip is not expected to preserve must be named explicitly in the test with a comment saying why, so that an intentional omission is visible and an accidental one fails.

This test would have caught all three defects. It should be written first and allowed to fail, so the fixes have a shared acceptance criterion.

Today those only appear in the BODY of the handful of dispatch-scoped events
that happen to carry them. Confirmed from one day of ex44 JSONL: agent_name
appears in 53 events across the whole fleet-day; every heartbeat, claim, and
state-transition event has neither. The dashboard therefore shows harness/model
for a worker only while a dispatch event is still inside the server ring buffer,
and null the rest of the time — visible live on 2026-08-16 for
claude-code-glm-4.7-tradegraph-1.

## Why the resource layer alone is not the answer

worker_telemetry_identity() (src/cli/mod.rs:849) resolves
agent = config.agent.default and model = that adapters declared model, ONCE at
boot, onto an immutable Resource. NEEDLE has model-based adapter routing
(config.agent.routing — set in this repos own .needle.yaml), so the adapter and
model actually dispatched can differ per bead from the configured default.

## Decision (ADR-016 §2)

needle.agent and needle.model appear at BOTH layers:
  - Resource: the configured default (process-invariant, useful when idle)
  - Log record: the adapter/model actually dispatched (wins over resource)

Document the precedence in the Semantic Mapping table so consumers do not guess.

## Deliverables

- Add needle.agent / needle.model to the attribute set in OtlpSink::emit_log
  (otlp.rs:1233), sourced from the workers current dispatch context rather
  than from config.
- Update the Semantic Mapping table in plan.md with the two-layer precedence.

## Acceptance

- A captured OTLP log record for a non-dispatch event (e.g. heartbeat.emitted)
  carries needle.agent and needle.model.
- When routing selects a non-default adapter, the record value reflects the
  adapter actually used, not config.agent.default.
- Dashboard shows Harness and Model for an idle worker, not just one mid-dispatch.

Blocked by needle-5359b52a (same emit path and same files — serialize to avoid
two workers editing src/telemetry/{mod,otlp}.rs concurrently).

See docs/adr/016-otlp-resource-propagation-and-roaming-worker-identity.md and
plan.md Phase 17 (17.2).
issue.title: Emit needle.agent and needle.model as per-record OTLP attributes, not only boot-time resource

The three backends are not feature-equivalent, and two of the gaps change fleet SAFETY rather than just convenience. These must be visible in operator-facing docs, not buried in code comments.

Gaps to document (docs/configuration.md and README backend section):
- Atomic mitosis is bf-ONLY. br and bead have no transactional batch, so split_bead falls back to the non-atomic default with its orphaned-child crash window (a crash between create and dep add leaves a child orphaned and the parent permanently blocked).
- Atomic server-side claim is bf- and bead-only. beads_rust has NO claim subcommand, so claim_auto is a read-then-write with a real TOCTOU window between ready and update. Two workers on the same beads_rust workspace can claim the same bead. This is the duplicate-claim failure mode CLAUDE.md already calls out as the real hazard in fleet dispatch.
- Velocity-aware claim scoring (--model/--harness/--harness-version) is bf-only; worker_sessions/velocity_stats rows are not written on other backends.

Deliverables:
- A capability matrix in docs/configuration.md matching ADR-013 section 2.
- `needle doctor` surfaces the active backend gaps, so an operator sees them without reading docs.

Acceptance criteria:
- An operator choosing a backend can see, before deploying a fleet, that beads_rust has no atomic claim.

See ADR-013 section 2 and Consequences.

issue.description:
src/bead_store/mod.rs:1550-1563 builds `create --title T --body B --json --silent [--labels a,b]`. bf 0.4.1 create accepts NONE of --body, --silent, --labels — only --title --description --type --priority --assignee --label (repeated) --json --envelope --no-auto-flush --no-progress --workspace. Verified via `bf create --help` on 2026-08-11.

BrCliBeadStore is the store EVERY worker path uses (worker/mod.rs:1385, supervisor/mod.rs:214, strand/explore.rs:71/:450, strand/splice.rs:747/:839/:999) and its discover() resolves `bf` FIRST — so the fleet runs the old br dialect against a binary that rejects it. BfCliBeadStore::create_bead (:2267-2280) already does it correctly but is only constructed in cli/mod.rs:997/:3384.

Blast radius: create_bead fails with a clap parse error (exit 2), and through the trait default split_bead (:646-668) that takes ALL mitosis child creation with it.

Deliverables:
- BrCliBeadStore::create_bead emits `--description` and repeated `--label`, matching BfCliBeadStore.
- Drop --json/--silent; bf create prints the bare ID on stdout already (the existing stdout.trim() parse is correct).

issue.description:
REFILE of the descriptor-type scope. Read this whole description; it is self-contained. Nothing here lives in a comment.

WHY THIS EXISTS: bf-2qm6r was filed as "split bead_store/mod.rs into per-backend files", then retargeted to this descriptor work via a COMMENT. NEEDLE prompts do not render bead comments (see bf-3b8x4), so the worker saw only the original description, did the split, and closed it (commit 82209c6). The split is genuinely DONE and correct. The descriptor scope was left unowned behind a closed bead. This bead re-files it with the scope in the description where a worker will actually see it.

DO NOT REDO THE SPLIT. src/bead_store/ is already mod.rs (1331 lines: trait, shared types, helpers) + br_cli.rs + bf_cli.rs + strategies.rs. That work is finished.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS: src/bead_store/strategies.rs (431 lines, no todo!/unimplemented!) defines all six operation-strategy enums — ClaimStrategy, ClaimAutoStrategy, SplitStrategy, CreateIdStrategy, LabelsStrategy, ImportStrategy. This bead consumes them; it does not redefine them.

DELIVERABLES

1. `BeadBackend` serde struct — a bead CLI described as DATA, so a new backend is a YAML file rather than a Rust impl. Fields:
   - name, binary, detect_paths (Vec<PathBuf>)
   - identity_pattern: regex matched against the binary --version output. This is load-bearing: ~/.local/bin/br is a shim that execs bf and reports "bf <version>", so a descriptor claiming beads_rust must reject it. Binding a store to a binary speaking another dialect is the exact defect ADR-013 section 5 documents.
   - version_command (default "--version")
   - verified_against + verified_on: the binary version/commit the descriptor was authored against, and the date. A host may run br 0.1.28 while upstream ships 0.2.22; a descriptor that does not say which it was written for is a guess.
   - operations: map of operation -> spec { argv template Vec<String>, optional strategy (from strategies.rs), parse shape, per-op timeout override }
   - capabilities: declared feature set (atomic_claim, transactional_batch, velocity_metadata)
   - quirks: version-scoped workarounds (see bf-1hm8g)
   - error markers: corruption / lock / sync-conflict string lists (see bf-1020b)

2. `builtin_bead_backends() -> Vec<BeadBackend>` returning the shipped descriptors, and `load_bead_backends(dir, &builtins) -> Result<HashMap<String, BeadBackend>>` merging user YAML from ~/.config/needle/bead-backends/, user files overriding builtins BY NAME.

   MODEL IT ON THE EXISTING PRECEDENT, do not invent a second pattern: src/dispatch/mod.rs:570-660 (`builtin_adapters` + `load_adapters`) does exactly this for agent harnesses. Same merge semantics, same YAML-in-a-directory convention, same override-by-name rule.

3. Config: `bead_cli.backend` (auto | descriptor name) + optional explicit `path`, in src/config/mod.rs alongside WorkspaceConfig (:289). Overridable per workspace in .needle.yaml.

4. VALIDATE AT LOAD TIME, NOT FIRST CLAIM. Reject: unknown strategy names, unresolvable {placeholders} in argv templates, missing required operations, absent identity_pattern. A malformed descriptor is now how a fleet loses the ability to claim beads — it must fail at startup naming the offending file and operation, not mid-dispatch.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- `grep -rn "struct BeadBackend\|fn load_bead_backends\|builtin_bead_backends" src/` returns real definitions.
- A user YAML in ~/.config/needle/bead-backends/ overrides a builtin of the same name.
- Each of the four validation failures above produces a distinct, actionable error naming the file.
- No behavior change yet: this bead adds the type and loader only. CliBeadStore (bf-1awps) consumes them.
- fmt + clippy + full suite green on iad-ci.

REFERENCE: docs/adr/013-pluggable-bead-cli-backends.md, Decision sections 1 and 2; docs/plan/plan.md Phase 16.1.

issue.description:
Grounded in memory reference_needle_lab_saturation_limits: idle roamers (Explore strand scanning
other workspaces for claimable beads) drive lab host load from ~4 to ~16 on a 12-core machine
while RAM barely moves -- CPU churn from repeated scanning of workspaces with no claimable work,
not real progress.

ExploreStrand (src/strand/explore.rs) currently has no notion of "this workspace/fleet has been
scanned N times in a row with zero claimable candidates found" -- it re-scans on the same cadence
regardless of hit rate. Add an adaptive backoff: track consecutive empty-scan cycles per worker
(in-memory is fine, does not need to survive restart) and geometrically increase the delay before
the next Explore pass (e.g. base interval up to some capped ceiling, e.g. 8x), resetting to base
the moment any candidate is found. Must not change the "no claimable beads" outcome-visibility for
strand escalation (Mend/Weave/etc. still evaluated in order) -- only the re-scan cadence within
Explore itself.

Acceptance criteria: a fixture simulating N consecutive empty Explore scans shows the effective
scan interval increasing up to the configured ceiling and resetting to base on the next
scan that finds a candidate; a regression test pins CPU-relevant behavior (call frequency, not
wall-clock) so it's testable without real sleeps.

issue.description:
Discovered 2026-07-28 while validating the GH #7-#11 fix (commit e97e88a / 4d8820f). `cargo test --lib` hangs indefinitely (near-zero CPU, zero log progress for 5+ minutes) on 4 tests in src/strand/explore.rs:
- strand::explore::tests::deadlock_scenario_assigned_beads_allow_advancement
- strand::explore::tests::deadlock_scenario_excluded_and_assigned_beads_allow_advancement
- strand::explore::tests::deadlock_scenario_excluded_beads_allow_advancement
- strand::explore::tests::nonexistent_workspace_path_returns_no_work

Reproduced independently in two separate environments:
1. Local (this server): cargo test --lib ran 50+ minutes with zero output progress before being killed (cgroup-limited run, CPUQuota=200%).
2. iad-ci workflow needle-ci-g7cqh (triggered by push of commit e97e88a to main): pod CPU usage measured at 1m (essentially idle) for 5+ minutes with these 4 tests stuck at 'has been running for over 60 seconds' and no further log lines appearing after. This is NOT slow-but-progressing (that would show real CPU usage from repeated lock-retry attempts) -- it looks like a genuine deadlock (a task waiting on something that never resolves), or a thread-pool-starvation cascade where these 4 stuck test threads exhaust the test harness's thread pool and block all other pending tests from ever running.

Root cause NOT yet investigated. src/strand/explore.rs has not been touched by any of the last 5+ commits (confirmed via git log), so this is pre-existing and unrelated to the GH #7-#11 fix or to any of the prerequisite compile-breakage fixes bundled in commit e97e88a (missing tsnet module wiring, MitosisConfig.max_depth, AgentAdapter test fixtures). Given CLAUDE.md documents that CI (needle-ci WorkflowTemplate) runs 'cargo test --lib' as its gating step, this hang means needle-ci will never reach the Succeeded phase for ANY future push until fixed -- it is not specific to this branch/commit.

The tests use a mock store factory (search 'DeadlockMockStoreFactory' in src/strand/explore.rs) and call strand.evaluate(&store).await inside a #[tokio::test] (default current-thread runtime). Worth checking: (a) whether ExploreStrand::evaluate or the mock factory has a genuine lock/channel deadlock under current-thread scheduling, (b) whether these tests ever passed in CI historically -- main did not even compile before this session's prerequisite fixes, so it is possible nobody has run the full suite to completion in some time and this has been silently broken for a while, (c) whether RUST_TEST_THREADS or --test-threads settings change the symptom.

Acceptance criteria: cargo test --lib completes (reaches 'test result: ... finished in Ns') without hanging, on both local and iad-ci; the 4 named tests either pass or are fixed/quarantined with a documented reason; needle-ci reaches Succeeded on a subsequent push.
issue.title: cargo test --lib hangs indefinitely on strand::explore deadlock_scenario_* tests

issue.description:
needle-ci is one monolithic pod that does setup, compile, test, a release
build and a GitHub publish, on every push to main -- guarded only by an
after-the-fact "does this tag already exist" check.

So roughly 95 percent of runs pay the full release cost, including
cargo build --release with lto=true and codegen-units=1 (the slowest possible
link configuration), only to discover the version did not change.

Do, in declarative-config k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/needle-workflowtemplate.yml:
- stage 1 verify: fmt, clippy, cargo check as a fast fail, then the test suite
- stage 2 release: only runs when the version in Cargo.toml differs from the

--release; a version bump still publishes exactly one release.

issue.close_reason: Fixed: Gate::validate is now async (#[async_trait]); CommandGate uses tokio::process::Command with kill_on_drop(true) instead of blocking std::process::Command. A slow gate command is now a genuine yield point tokio::time::timeout can actually abandon and kill, not just report late. Verified with command_gate_slow_command_is_killed_when_dropped_mid_flight and handle_with_cancellation_kills_a_slow_verification_gate_command (end-to-end repro of the original scenario). 405 targeted tests pass. See ADR-009 addendum, plan.md 13.6a.
issue.description:
Discovered 2026-07-28 while adding tests for bf-3pc1r/bf-j8o7w (GH #8/#9, commit e97e88a). CommandGate::run_command (src/validation/mod.rs) calls the fully synchronous, blocking std::process::Command::output() with no .await point during a gate command's execution. tokio::time::timeout's Timeout::poll polls the wrapped future first and only checks its deadline if that poll returns Pending -- so a wrapped future with no yield point during a slow blocking segment always completes before the deadline check can matter.

Net effect: validation.outcome_timeout_seconds (now configurable per GH #8) can only observe, after the fact, that a gate command ran longer than the configured timeout -- it cannot actually cut the command off mid-execution the way its role (outcome-handler gate timeout) implies. A gate command that hangs or runs very long will block the whole outcome-handling task for its full duration regardless of the configured timeout value.

First discovered via a broken test: an initial version of a handle_with_cancellation test used a slow verification: gate command (sleep 2) to try to trigger a 1s configured timeout, and it failed on iad-ci (workflow needle-ci-g7cqh) because the gate ran to completion (2s) before the timeout could ever be observed. The test was corrected (commit 4d8820f) to use a genuinely-async slow store operation instead, which does correctly demonstrate the config value is honored for the *other* (already-async) operations handle() performs -- just not for gate command execution itself.

Suggested fix: run CommandGate's std::process::Command::output() inside tokio::task::spawn_blocking, so the returned JoinHandle future is a genuine yield point tokio::time::timeout can race against. The underlying OS process would still need its own kill-on-timeout handling (spawn_blocking alone doesn't kill the child process if the JoinHandle is abandoned) to avoid leaking a runaway subprocess after the outer timeout fires -- worth designing deliberately rather than bolting on.

Acceptance criteria: a gate command configured to run longer than validation.outcome_timeout_seconds is actually interrupted (its OS process killed, not just outlived) at approximately the configured timeout, with a regression test proving it (a slow gate command + short configured timeout observed to return around the timeout, not after the full command duration).
issue.title: outcome_timeout_seconds cannot preempt a slow gate command (blocking subprocess, no async yield point)
