issue.description:
## Problem

ADR-016 (docs/adr/016-otlp-resource-propagation-and-roaming-worker-identity.md)
Root Cause B: the dashboard's first-choice source for the "Repo" field is the
per-record log attribute `workspace` (server-side `normalize_otlp_log`:
`attrs.get("workspace") or data.get("workspace") or
resource.get("needle.workspace")`). `OtlpSink::emit_log` does set that
attribute -- but only `if let Some(ref workspace) = event.workspace`, and
`TelemetryEvent.workspace` is hardcoded to `None` at every emit site:

- `Telemetry::emit` -- src/telemetry/mod.rs:3323 (line numbers as of
  2026-08-16; needle-a8a6e16e and needle-501aa991 landed since ADR-016 was
  written, re-check before starting)
- `Telemetry::emit_sync` -- src/telemetry/mod.rs:3488

The field is declared in `TelemetryEvent` (mod.rs:71), documented in
plan.md's telemetry module spec, filterable via the query layer
(mod.rs:4023), and serialized into the file sink -- and is never once
populated.

This is half of Root Cause C too: even with Root Cause A fixed
(needle-a8a6e16e, closed), the boot-time `needle.workspace` Resource
attribute is frozen at launch and wrong for a roaming worker (`needle run
-w` is "NOT an exclusive scope" -- the Explore strand claims beads in
other repos under the same process). A resource-only fix would make
"Repo" confidently wrong instead of blank, which the ADR judges worse
than `Unknown`.

## Decision (from ADR-016)

> `Telemetry` gains a current-workspace cell that the worker updates when
> a claim binds it to a workspace. `emit`/`emit_sync` read that cell
> instead of writing `None`. `Bead.workspace` (src/claim/mod.rs:609) is
> already the authoritative source and is known before dispatch, so no
> new plumbing crosses a module boundary. Basename-only reduction stays
> where 519468a put it, in `workspace_label`, so full filesystem paths
> still never reach the browser.

Per the ADR's semantic table, `workspace` (repo basename) lives on the
**record only** -- not the Resource -- because it changes every time the
worker roams and a Resource value is structurally incapable of being
correct.

## Acceptance criteria

- `Telemetry` has a current-workspace cell, updated when a claim binds
  the worker to a workspace (source: `Bead.workspace`, claim/mod.rs:609).
- `emit`/`emit_sync` read that cell instead of hardcoding `None`.
- Verified per ADR-016 Decision #5 (wire capture, not a green test): a
  raw OTLP payload from a real `needle` binary shows the `workspace`
  per-record attribute as a basename, changing across a session as the
  worker roams between repos -- not a single frozen value.
- No full filesystem path reaches the browser/dashboard contract --
  basename-only, matching `workspace_label`'s existing reduction.

## Related

- needle-a8a6e16e (closed) -- Root Cause A, the exporter-wrapper fix this
  builds on.
- needle-501aa991 (closed) -- prior incomplete attempt; see ADR-016 "Why
  the previous fix did not land" for why it didn't move the dashboard.
- needle-5d246a6d (open) -- sibling bead for the needle.agent/needle.model
  per-record half of the same ADR decision. Consider landing together.
- needle-bb5b32f3 (open) -- provider attribute, same pattern, filed
  separately.
issue.title: Populate TelemetryEvent.workspace at emit time (ADR-016 Decision 3)

Found during the ADR-002 field-guide independent review (2026-08-12), recorded as I4.

add_dependency does not validate kind, and the insert uses INSERT OR IGNORE (src/service/dependencies.rs:128-137), which swallows the DB CHECK (kind IN ('blocks','relates_to')) violation at src/store/migrations.rs:162.

Verified empirically:

  Added dependency: t-fc96fb48 related to t-1294272c
  exit=0
  $ sqlite3 .beads/beads.db 'SELECT * FROM dependencies'
  t-fc96fb48|t-aa8b9d29|blocks     # the bogus edge was silently dropped

Kind validation exists only on the dry-run path (src/service/dryrun.rs:331-334), so --dry-run rejects what the real command accepts.

Fix: validate kind before insert and return exit 4 on an unknown kind; reserve INSERT OR IGNORE for the genuine idempotency case.

issue.description:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND REPRODUCED 2026-08-07. Supersedes the "wall-clock timing"
theory recorded on bf-2mp0y — that was wrong.

The real error, captured by temporarily replacing the discarded Result with a
print:

  failed to spawn bf subprocess: ["list", "--json", "--limit", "999999"]
  Caused by:
      Text file busy (os error 26)
      root = Os { code: 26, kind: ExecutableFileBusy, message: "Text file busy" }

REPRODUCTION (deterministic enough to iterate on):

  cargo test --lib bead_store::tests -- --test-threads=32

run in a loop 40x produced 15 failing runs — a 37.5 percent per-run failure
rate. It does NOT reproduce at default thread counts, which is why the suite
looks green locally and red on the smaller CI node.

MECHANISM. These tests write a fake bf/br shell script, chmod 0755 it, then
execute it. Linux fails execve with ETXTBSY if ANY process holds the file open
for writing. Rust opens files O_CLOEXEC, but fork/posix_spawn still leaves a
window: a concurrently spawning test forks, the child inherits the writing
testfixture fd, and until that child reaches execve the script counts as "open
for writing". Any test exec-ing its own freshly written script in that window
gets ETXTBSY. 11 sites in this file write+chmod+exec a script, so the window is
hit often once tests run concurrently.

WHY THE SYMPTOM LOOKED UNRELATED. In each of these tests the workspace and the
args file are the SAME directory (workspace = tmp_dir.path(), args_file =
tmp_dir.path().join(..)), and the spawn error is discarded by
"let _ = store.list_all().await;". The fake script therefore never runs, never
writes the args file, and the next line panics on
read_to_string(&args_file).unwrap() with a bare
Os { code: 2, kind: NotFound }. The genuine ETXTBSY is thrown away one line
earlier. Every CI failure has been reported by this misleading NotFound.

AFFECTED TESTS (observed failing across 40 runs):
  7x bf_cli_bead_store_list_all_passes_explicit_limit
  4x br_cli_bead_store_ready_passes_explicit_limit
  2x br_cli_bead_store_ready_filters_by_exclude_ids
  2x bf_cli_bead_store_ready_passes_explicit_limit
  2x bf_cli_bead_store_ready_filters_by_exclude_ids
  1x br_cli_bead_store_list_all_passes_large_explicit_limit

NOT ONLY A TEST BUG. run_bf_in (~line 1591) and run_br_in (~line 567) both do
cmd.spawn()? with no ETXTBSY handling, and so do run_bf_batch (~864) and
run_bf_claim (~926). NEEDLE hot-reloads its own binaries and upgrades bf in
place, so a worker that spawns bf or needle while that file is being rewritten
hits exactly this errno in production and fails the operation outright.

The fix already exists in this same file and was simply never generalised:
spawn_version_check (~line 68) retries raw_os_error()==Some(26) five times with
a 20ms backoff, and its doc comment describes this precise race. Only the
--version path is protected.

Solution tracked separately.
issue.notes:
[migrated labels from bf-37hoj]
ci, deferred, tests, umbrella
issue.title: ETXTBSY on subprocess spawn: run_br_in/run_bf_in never retry 'Text file busy', flaking 6 bead_store tests

issue.close_reason: Implemented repeat_interval gating for first_failure_only mitosis, skipped repeat ticks for mitosis-depth beads, added default coverage, and verified cargo fmt --check, all 72 mitosis unit tests, config default test, and cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings.
issue.description:
## Problem

`MitosisConfig.first_failure_only` (default: true) means mitosis only fires on failure #1.
Beads that fail repeatedly after the first attempt loop forever with thousands of failures
and no re-split. Seen in practice: bf-27p7 at 1650+ failures, mta-my-way-rq9 at 2050+.

`force_failure_threshold` exists but fires on every failure >= N — too noisy.

## Work

### 1. `src/config/mod.rs` — add `repeat_interval` to `MitosisConfig`

Add field:
```rust
/// Re-run mitosis every N consecutive failures after the first (0 = disabled).
/// Fires at failure_count == 1, 1+N, 1+2N, ...
/// Only when force_failure_threshold == 0.
/// Beads already carrying a mitosis-depth label are skipped.
#[serde(default)]
pub repeat_interval: u32,
```

### 2. `src/mitosis/mod.rs` — update failure-count gate

In the `else if self.config.first_failure_only && failure_count != 1` branch, extend to
also allow firing when `repeat_interval > 0` and `(failure_count - 1) % repeat_interval == 0`
AND the bead does not have a `mitosis-depth:*` label. Keep the existing early-return pattern.

### 3. Unit tests in `src/mitosis/mod.rs`

- `repeat_interval_triggers_at_correct_counts`: fires at 1, 1+N, 1+2N; skips all others
- `repeat_interval_skips_max_depth_beads`: bead with `mitosis-depth:1` label + repeat tick → skipped
- `repeat_interval_zero_preserves_first_failure_only`: interval=0, first_failure_only=true → only fires at 1

## Acceptance criteria

- `cargo fmt` + `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean
- All existing mitosis tests pass
- New unit tests pass
- Config `[mitosis]\nrepeat_interval = 50` causes re-split at failure 51, 101, etc.
issue.title: Mitosis: add repeat_interval to trigger re-split on consecutive failures

issue.description:
Compounding half of GH #12 (https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE/issues/12), same report as bf-12bim (reap sweep). Full rationale: ADR-010 (docs/adr/010-supervisor-zombie-reaping.md), plan.md Phase 14.2.

Confirmed against source: registry::is_pid_alive (src/registry/mod.rs:28-52) checks liveness via kill(pid, 0) == 0 (with errno ESRCH/EPERM disambiguation). kill(pid, 0) succeeds for a zombie (state Z) exactly as it does for a genuinely running process — a zombie still holds a PID table entry, it just hasn't been reaped yet (see bf-12bim). This is not a hypothetical concern: Supervisor::tick() (src/supervisor/mod.rs:308-336) filters registered workers with is_pid_alive(w.pid) (line 316) to compute alive_count, then gates new spawns on alive_count >= self.config.max_workers (line 335). So every unreaped worker zombie is counted as alive by the supervisor's own tick, artificially inflating alive_count and potentially blocking new worker spawns at exactly the moment real capacity exists. The reporter's issue explicitly connects this to a 'false max_workers capacity and silent hung supervise logs' observation during their cutover soak (compounded on their host by an unrelated large zombie population from PID 1 not reaping its own children).

strand::mend's liveness check (src/strand/mend.rs:707) also calls registry::is_pid_alive and inherits this same bug.

Suggested fix (decision in ADR-010): on Linux, additionally check /proc/<pid>/stat's process-state field (the character after the second ')' in the comm field, robust to command names containing parentheses) and treat state Z as NOT alive, even though kill(pid, 0) still succeeds for it. Fall back to today's kill(pid, 0)-only behavior on non-Linux platforms (no /proc on macOS) and whenever /proc/<pid>/stat is unreadable for any reason (permissions, race with process exit) — never MORE strict than today's check, only additionally strict for the one case (Z) that today's check gets provably wrong.

Explicitly out of scope (per ADR-010): src/cli/mod.rs has its own separate, simpler duplicate is_pid_alive (kill(pid,0)==0, no errno handling) used for needle status/needle cleanup display/filtering, not supervisor capacity gating. It has the same zombie blind spot in principle but fixing it is not necessary to resolve GH #12's reported impact — leave it as a smaller, separate follow-up if status/cleanup output for zombies becomes its own complaint.

Acceptance criteria:
- registry::is_pid_alive returns false for a deliberately-created, deliberately-unreaped zombie PID on Linux.
- Behavior unchanged for non-Linux platforms and for genuinely-alive/genuinely-dead PIDs on all platforms (existing liveness tests still pass).
- Regression test reproducing the reporter's capacity-hang scenario: a zombie worker in the registry no longer counts toward alive_count in Supervisor::tick().
- cargo test --lib passes; no clippy warnings; needle-ci green on push.
issue.title: is_pid_alive treats zombie workers as alive, fooling supervisor capacity accounting (GH #12, compounding)

Created scripts/verify-shipped-commit.sh that builds HEAD in an isolated detached worktree (immune to sibling workers' uncommitted edits), then updated .needle.yaml to enable the gate with outcome_timeout_seconds raised to 300. Verified end-to-end: current HEAD passes the gate, a deliberately broken commit fails correctly with exit code 101. issue.description:
## The pattern

Two P1 beads were closed in a single session with their own stated acceptance
criteria demonstrably unmet. Both shipped real, substantial code — this is not
agents doing nothing and lying about it:

- needle-04df9025 "Test OTLP attributes at the transport seam". Acceptance said
  "CI green on iad-ci (do not run cargo test locally)". Closed 2026-08-16T05:11Z.
  The committed test file did not compile — 24 errors — so the test target was
  never built and not one assertion ever ran. `cargo install --git` from the
  public repo was broken for external users at the same time.
- needle-ea87796e "checkpoint references generation objects not in git". Closed
  2026-08-16T14:03Z with a 220-line publish script, a pre-commit hook, docs and
  an AGENTS.md entry. The guard's trigger is too narrow, so a commit staging a
  root-object deletion with no pointer change is waved through — reproducing the
  exact defect the bead existed to prevent. Verified against a fresh clone.

## Documentation cannot fix this

needle-04df9025's acceptance criterion literally said "CI green on iad-ci".
NEEDLE's CLAUDE.md says "If CI fails, add the log output as a note to the bead
and do **not** close it." The instruction existed, was specific, was in context,
and was not followed. Adding another note asking agents to try harder is the
control that has already failed twice; the fix has to be mechanical.

## The mechanism already exists and is switched off

`OutcomeHandler::handle_success` (src/outcome/mod.rs:362) runs validation gates
on agent success BEFORE accepting closure, and `handle_gate_failure` reopens the
bead if the agent closed it, then releases it. That is exactly the undo needed
for a premature close, already implemented and tested.

This workspace's own `.needle.yaml` has:

    verification: []
    gates: []

So every close is accepted unconditionally. NEEDLE is not dogfooding the one
feature that addresses its own worst failure mode.

Note `verify_shipped_work` (src/validation/shipped_work.rs) does NOT cover this.
It compares a pre-dispatch snapshot to post state to catch an agent that shipped
nothing. Both failures above shipped plenty; what shipped just did not work.

## The constraint that makes the naive fix wrong

A gate must NOT simply run a build in `bead.workspace`. Measured in the live
shared checkout on 2026-08-16:

    cargo check --all-targets   ->  75 errors, elapsed 15.80s

The errors are a concurrent worker's in-flight refactor (Telemetry gained
`current_adapter`/`current_model`; new EventKind variants not yet matched
everywhere). Uncommitted, legitimate, mid-task work. A workspace-wide build gate
would therefore fail EVERY bead closure in this repo right now and release them
all — a thundering herd caused by one unrelated worker's editor state. Multiple
NEEDLE workers share one checkout by design (ADR-015), so this is the normal
condition, not an edge case.

The gate must verify what was SHIPPED — the commit — in isolation from the
shared working tree.

## Proposed design

A gate command that builds HEAD in a throwaway detached worktree:

    git worktree add --detach "$TMP" HEAD
    (cd "$TMP" && cargo check --all-targets)
    git worktree remove "$TMP" --force

This verifies exactly the artifact the acceptance criteria talk about, is immune
to sibling workers' uncommitted files, and would have caught needle-04df9025
directly — its failure was a test target that did not compile, which is why
`--all-targets` is required rather than `--lib --bins`.

Cost is acceptable: 15.8s warm for the check itself, and a shared
CARGO_TARGET_DIR keeps the worktree build incremental.

`validation.outcome_timeout_seconds` defaults to 50 and wraps the whole handler
including gates. It must be raised — the code comment at src/outcome/mod.rs:309
already anticipates this ("a gate running a real verification workload ... needs
minutes, not seconds", GitHub issue jedarden/NEEDLE#8).

Gate config shape (`GateConfig::Command`, src/validation/mod.rs:97):

    validation:
      outcome_timeout_seconds: <raised>
    gates:
      - type: command
        commands:
          - scripts/verify-shipped-commit.sh

## Deliverables

- A verification script that builds HEAD in an isolated worktree and cleans up
  after itself, including on failure.
- Enable it in this workspace's `.needle.yaml` gates, with a raised
  `outcome_timeout_seconds`.
- Roll out deliberately: turning this on while main is red will release every
  bead that tries to close. Confirm HEAD builds first.
- Consider whether the gate belongs in other Rust workspaces on the fleet; the
  pattern is not NEEDLE-specific, only observed here first.

## Acceptance

- An agent that closes a bead whose HEAD does not compile has that bead reopened
  and released automatically, with a VerificationFailed telemetry event.
- A sibling worker's uncommitted broken edits do NOT cause a gate failure.
- Demonstrated end to end on a deliberately broken commit.

## Refs

needle-04df9025, needle-ea87796e (both reopened after being closed prematurely);
src/outcome/mod.rs:362 handle_success; src/validation/mod.rs:97 GateConfig;
ADR-015 shared-checkout model.
issue.title: Premature bead closure is systemic: enable a validation gate that verifies the SHIPPED COMMIT, not the shared worktree

issue.description:
~/.local/bin/br is a shell shim that logs the caller and execs ~/.local/bin/bf. The real beads_rust binary is ~/.cargo/bin/br v0.1.28. So `which br` returns something that speaks the bf dialect — this is exactly how ADR-013 section 5 went unnoticed for as long as it did.

A resolver that finds `br` on PATH and assumes beads_rust will bind the beads_rust adapter to bead-forge all over again, in a new place.

Deliverables:
- After resolving a candidate binary, VERIFY the backend identity rather than trusting the filename. `br --version` on the shim prints `bf <version>` (it execs bf), so a version-string check is sufficient and cheap — but confirm that empirically before relying on it.
- On mismatch (filename says br, identity says bf), fail loudly with an actionable message naming both paths. Do not silently fall back.
- Same check for a bf-named binary that is actually something else.

Acceptance criteria:
- A test with a fixture shim (a script execing a different fake binary) proves the mismatch is detected and reported, not silently accepted.
- The error message names the resolved path AND the identity actually found.

See ADR-013 section 5 and Evidence.

issue.description:
New src/bead_store/bead_cli.rs implementing the existing BeadStore trait against bead-rs (`bead`). Surface enumerated from ~/bead-rs/src/cli.rs at commit fa30574.

Dialect specifics (each differs from bf in a way that fails loudly at runtime and silently in review):
- claim/release/clear_assignee: plain `update --status ... --assignee ...` / `update --status open --clear-assignee`. bead-rs UpdateOptions (cli.rs:444) KEPT the --assignee that bf 0.4.1 removed, so these are SIMPLER here than on bf — no batch emulation needed.
- claim_auto: `claim --assignee A --json`. Omit --model/--harness/--harness-version — bead-rs ClaimOptions (cli.rs:370) does not accept them. Selection falls back to bead-rs own --policy (default fifo-v1).
- create_bead: `--description` (not --body), repeated `--label`, no --json. bead-rs create prints the bare issue ID on stdout.
- add_dependency: `--kind blocks` (not --type). Confirm positional order against the installed binary before landing.
- full_rebuild: bead-rs `sync --import-only` REQUIRES --input plus exactly one of --restore-into-empty / --merge (SyncCommand, cli.rs:667). The current bare call would fail.
- list/show/update --status/reopen/close --reason/label add|remove/doctor [--repair]/sync --flush-only all match and need no special handling.
- split_bead: deliberately NOT overridden. bead-rs has no `batch` subcommand, so it inherits the non-atomic trait default (:646-668) and its documented orphaned-child crash window. Log at split time that the atomic path is unavailable on this backend.

Acceptance criteria:
- Every trait method implemented; no todo!()/unimplemented!().
- Known limitations (no atomic split, no velocity-scoring metadata) are logged at runtime, not silently swallowed.
- fmt + clippy + full suite green on iad-ci.

  k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/, triggered by changes to Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock or
  ci/Dockerfile.ci*
- pin a semver tag, never latest and never a bare git SHA
- switch needle-ci's container image to it and delete the inline apt/rustup/gh
  install block

Blocked by the Cargo.lock bead: Dockerfile.ci-deps does COPY Cargo.toml Cargo.lock.

issue.description:
## Problem

`config::Backend` (src/config/mod.rs:436) derives Debug/Clone/PartialEq/Eq but
has no `Display` impl, unlike its sibling `config::BeadBackend`
(src/config/mod.rs:391), which does.

This was one of the five compile errors that made main unbuildable
(fixed in b538d06): src/canary/mod.rs used `%backend_type` in a `tracing::info!`
and `{}` in a `bail!`, both of which require Display.

## Current workaround

b538d06 debug-formats it instead — `?backend_type` in the tracing call and
`{:?}` in the bail. That compiles and is correct, but it is inconsistent:
the same log line now prints `backend=bead-forge` (BeadBackend, Display) next to
`resolved_backend=Bf` (Backend, Debug), and the same split shows up in the
"binary not found" error text.

The workaround was deliberately confined to src/canary/mod.rs rather than fixing
it at the source, because src/config/mod.rs had ~44 lines of another worker's
uncommitted in-flight edits at the time and committing that file would have
swept up unrelated work.

## Deliverables

- Add `impl std::fmt::Display for Backend` in src/config/mod.rs, mirroring the
  BeadBackend impl and using the same user-facing spellings
  (Backend::Bf -> "bead-forge", Backend::Bead -> "bead-rs").
- Revert the canary workaround to `%backend_type` / `{}` and drop the
  explanatory comment above the tracing call.

## Acceptance

- `cargo check --lib` and `cargo clippy --lib` clean.
- The canary "bead backend validated" log line renders both backend fields in
  the same human-readable spelling.

issue.close_reason: Fixed in bead-rs 9836b07: checkpoint export/import now preserves external references transactionally, with active round-trip conformance coverage and full gates passing.
issue.description:
Found during the ADR-002 field-guide independent review (2026-08-12). NOT previously recorded; discovered while auditing the full flush/restore path.

Reproduced with bead 0.1.1 in disposable workspaces:
  source: 2 issues, 3 labels, 1 blocks edge, 1 issue_data namespace, 1 external_reference, 2 events
  bead sync flush-only, then bead sync import-only --input CP --restore-into-empty --actor X
  restored: labels 3 OK, dependencies 1 OK, events 2 OK, issue_data 0 LOST, external_references 0 LOST, revision 3 -> 1 LOST

The checkpoint contains only issue and event record types. Labels and dependencies survive because they are carried inline as members of the issue record. There is no record type for external references and no member for them on the issue record, so every (namespace, key, value) written through bead ref add is destroyed by a flush/restore cycle.

WHY THIS IS THE MOST SEVERE OF THE ROUND-TRIP LOSSES: research/specs/native-field-guide-v1.md L168-170 and L213 make external references THE public mechanism binding rehydrated beads back to their source tracker IDs. The same document's rehearsal procedure flushes a checkpoint and restores it into a fresh workspace. As implemented, that rehearsal silently destroys the entire traceability chain it exists to prove.

Fix: carry external references in the checkpoint (either as an inline issue member alongside labels/dependencies, or as a distinct record_type) and write them on both import paths. Add round-trip coverage - see the conformance-test bead.
issue.notes:
[migrated comment from bf-53b91, 2026-08-13T11:25:17.738207111Z, author cli]
Round-3 review (2026-08-13): the restore path is genuinely fixed and this bead is correctly closed — a flush/restore-into-empty round trip on a build of e5141b9 preserved external references 1 -> 1. However the fix commit 9836b07 relocated the loss to the merge path: reconcile_and_merge now DELETEs external_references and reinserts only what the incoming record carries, so merging any checkpoint without the member (including every checkpoint released 0.1.1 can produce) empties them. Tracked as bf-1cwrc; do not treat this bead's closure as covering --merge.

[migrated labels from bf-53b91]
bead-rs, field-guide-review, rehydration-blocker
issue.title: bead-rs: external references are silently dropped by the checkpoint round-trip

Two `needle-ci` runs failed on iad-ci with the same signature, 9h and 11h
before 2026-08-06 12:35Z:

- `needle-ci-vnmhd` — workflow message "Max duration limit exceeded",
  node exit **101**
- `needle-ci-x2wx2` — identical

Exit 101 is the Rust convention for a panic / `cargo test` failure, so this
is a real red suite, not just the duration cap. The duration message means
the run also hit the workflow's max-duration before finishing.

Relates to the epic bf-21tze ("cut NEEDLE CI from a ~50min red run to a
<10min green run") — this bead records the concrete current failure so the
epic has a reproducible starting point rather than a general description.

## Also observed: needle-ci pile-up

At 12:35Z there were **four** needle-ci workflows queued simultaneously
(`needle-ci-8x2jj` 76m, `-f46kr` 69m, `-kz4qz` 62m, `-xt8tz` 62m), none of
them able to schedule a pod. Each push spawns another run while the previous
ones are still queued, so the queue grows faster than it drains. Consider a
concurrency limit / `synchronization` semaphore on the needle-ci template so
only one run is in flight per branch.

## Reproducing

Pod logs are gone (`podGC: OnPodCompletion`). Resubmit with a
`podGC: OnWorkflowCompletion` override, or stream logs while running.

issue.description:
Found 2026-08-02 upgrading ex44 to v0.2.16.

'needle upgrade' downloaded 0.2.16, ran canary validation, scored 0/4 and
rejected the binary. The rejection is NOT a regression in the new build — the
canary expectations under ~/.needle/canary/expected/ are dated 2026-03-21 and
have not tracked bead-forge's vocabulary since.

expected/canary-bzl.yaml (the happy-path test) asserts:

    final_status: done

bead-forge has no 'done' status. Statuses actually in use across real
workspaces are: open, in_progress, blocked, closed, completed, pending, ready.
A closed bead reports 'closed'. NEEDLE knows this — src/types/mod.rs carries the
comment "br show --json emits 'closed' for done beads. Treat as equivalent".
So canary-bzl is unsatisfiable by ANY needle binary, old or new, and the canary
gate can never pass.

The observed run looked behaviourally fine: canary-bzl closed, canary-nnw
closed, canary-8ej blocked, canary-atw in_progress. All four were still scored
as failures, so the other three expectations are likely stale in the same way
(canary-8ej wants final_status 'open' plus a 'failure-count:1' label;
canary-nnw wants 'open' for a timeout).

Impact: the upgrade path on any host with a canary workspace is permanently
blocked, and the failure presents as 'the new binary is bad' rather than 'the
test fixtures rotted'. bench has no canary workspace, so it promoted 0.2.16
straight to :stable and its workers hot-reloaded correctly — good evidence the
binary itself is fine.

Not urgent for correctness on ex44: it still has the deprecated br shim at
~/.local/bin/br, so its 0.2.14 workers' 'br close' continues to work. The cost
is that ex44 stays on old binaries.

Fix direction: refresh the four expected/*.yaml against current bead-forge
vocabulary, and add an assertion that each expected final_status is a status
bf can actually produce, so this rots loudly next time. Also surface per-test
detail — 'needle canary --status' only prints channel state, giving no clue
which expectation failed or why.

Acceptance: 'needle upgrade' on ex44 passes canary and promotes to :stable.
issue.notes:
[migrated comment from bf-5my6q, 2026-08-02T19:53:30.387684238Z, author cli]
Fuller diagnosis 2026-08-02 — NOT a fixture-only fix. Five independent defects; the gate has almost certainly never worked.

1. NO BEAD RESET. CanaryRunner::run() has no reset/seed step — grep for reset_bead/seed/set_status in src/canary/mod.rs returns nothing. The four beads keep whatever terminal state the last run left (now: canary-bzl=closed, canary-nnw=closed, canary-8ej=blocked, canary-atw=in_progress). A worker cannot claim a closed bead, so later runs do nothing.

2. RACE. run_test() spawns `needle run --workspace ... --count 1` WITHOUT NEEDLE_INNER=1. That form detaches into tmux and returns immediately — the upgrade output prints "Started worker ... in tmux session / Attach with: tmux attach -t ...". So child.try_wait() returns exit 0 within milliseconds and get_actual_outcome() reads the bead long before any agent work. The exit code compared for Success/Failure is the launcher's, not the agent's.

3. StateMachine UNIMPLEMENTED. get_actual_outcome() hardcodes state_transitions: Vec::new() ("Not tracked in basic canary tests"). outcomes_match() does transitions.iter().all(|t| actual.state_transitions.contains(t)); against an always-empty vec any non-empty expected list is unsatisfiable. canary-atw could only pass with zero transitions, i.e. vacuously.

4. STALE VOCABULARY. ExpectedOutcome::default_final_status() returns "done", and expected/canary-bzl.yaml asserts final_status: done. bead-forge has no 'done' status (open/in_progress/blocked/closed/completed/pending/ready). The rot is in the source default too, so omitting the field does not help.

5. USES br. get_actual_outcome() runs Command::new(&self.br_path).args(["show", id, "--json"]). On a host without the deprecated br shim the canary errors instead of validating — same root cause as bf-15tys.

Consequence: the canary cannot pass for ANY binary, which is why 'needle upgrade' on ex44 rejected v0.2.16 at 0/4. Nothing is wrong with that build — bench has no canary workspace, promoted it, and both workers hot-reloaded and now emit 'bf close'.

Real fix spans all five points plus refreshed fixtures plus a CI cycle — materially more than editing YAML. Until then the gate protects nothing; it is a permanent block that presents as "the new binary is bad".
issue.title: Canary expectations are stale (expect status 'done'), so every upgrade is rejected 0/4 on ex44

issue.close_reason: Investigation complete. Root cause identified: Resolve strand spawns claude processes without setting working directory in src/strand/resolve.rs:333. When supervisor starts from $HOME, workers inherit $HOME, and Resolve-spawned claude processes get cwd=$HOME. The strand is not currently in the active waterfall, but was active during the 2026-07-29 incident. Processes hung for 11-13 hours without being reaped. Fix: add .current_dir(workspace) to Command::new("claude") call. Bead updated with full technical analysis.
issue.description:
Observed 2026-07-29 ~13:35 EDT on lab (100.81.129.38): load average 304-308 on a 12-core box (worse than any prior recorded fleet incident, including the 07-28 17-pinned-worker crisis that peaked at load 200+). vmstat confirmed it was real, not cosmetic: procs.r (runnable) was 281-295, %sy (kernel time) pegged at 100%, %us at 0% — pure context-switch thrashing (70-100k switches/sec), not actual work. Memory/swap were fine (34/62Gi used, 254Mi swap) — ruled out memory pressure as the driver.

Root cause of the load: found via `ps -eo comm --no-headers | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn` — 115 separate 'claude' processes, vastly more than the 4 live 'needle run' supervisors present at the time, and far beyond any previously recorded fleet size. Per-process inspection (`readlink /proc/<pid>/cwd`) showed EVERY one of the 115 had cwd = /home/coding — the bare home directory, not any project repo/workspace. Elapsed times ranged 41735-48134s (11.6-13.4h), clustered into groups sharing identical spawn timestamps (consistent with programmatic mass-spawn over time, not 115 separate manual terminal sessions). All 115 shared PPID = the tmux server hosting the needle-supervisor session (normal tmux pane-reparenting, not itself meaningful).

IMPORTANT — this is distinct from bf-12bim (supervisor zombie/defunct-child non-reaping, GH #12): these were LIVE, RUNNING processes, not <defunct> zombies. Proof: `pkill -9 -x claude` successfully killed all of them immediately (zombies are already dead and cannot be re-killed) — pgrep -c -x claude went to 0/1, then within seconds needle supervise's autoscaler correctly spun up 3 fresh workers with correct cwd (~/claude-print, ~/miroir, ~/drawrace), confirming the supervisor's spawn/autoscale logic itself is healthy. run-queue and load recovered immediately (vmstat procs.r dropped to 1-3, idle% to 82%, free memory 4.7Gi -> 24Gi).

NOT YET ROOT-CAUSED — open research questions for whoever picks this up:
1. What code path spawns a 'claude' process with cwd left at the operator's home directory instead of cd'ing into the target workspace first? Check src/dispatch/mod.rs (run_process) and src/supervisor/mod.rs (spawn_worker) for any fallback/default path taken when workspace resolution fails, is empty, or a workspace arg is omitted — does it silently fall back to the process's inherited cwd instead of erroring?
2. Why did ~115 of these accumulate over ~11-13h without anything reaping/killing them? Is there a retry loop that spawns a new claude on every tick without checking/killing the previous attempt if it hasn't exited? Cross-check against bf-1ynu9 (supervisor spawns workers via current_exe() instead of PATH lookup) and bf-12bim (zombie reaping) for any shared code path, though neither obviously explains a home-dir cwd.
3. What were these processes actually doing/blocked on for 11+ hours? If any `~/.needle/logs/needle-*.stderr.log` or claude-side transcript/session logs exist for PIDs active in the 2026-07-29 ~00:48-13:35 EDT window, check whether they show a real dispatch attempt that hung (e.g. waiting on stdin, a broken PTY, a network call that never returns) versus something spawned outside the normal dispatch path entirely (health check, canary, some other subprocess call to the 'claude' binary).
4. Is this reproducible on demand, or was it a one-off (e.g. triggered by one of the 07-28 fleet collapse/relaunch cycles leaving these behind)? Check whether the same pattern (claude count wildly disproportionate to needle process count, cwd=$HOME) recurs after future collapses/relaunches.

Fingerprint to grep for if this recurs: `ps -eo comm | sort | uniq -c` showing claude count >> needle process count, combined with `/proc/<pid>/cwd` resolving to the operator home directory across the cluster, and elapsed times all much older than any live needle process's uptime.
issue.notes:
Investigation complete. Found bug in src/strand/resolve.rs lines 333-339: Command::new("claude") without .current_dir(). This spawns claude processes that inherit the parent process's cwd. When supervisor starts from $HOME, workers inherit $HOME, and Resolve-strand-spawned claude processes get cwd=$HOME. 

Key findings:
1. ROOT CAUSE: resolve.rs invoke_resolver() spawns claude without setting cwd
2. NOT CURRENTLY ACTIVE: ResolveStrand is NOT in the active strand waterfall (StrandRunner::from_config only includes: Pluck, Mend, Explore, Weave, Unravel, Pulse, Reflect, Splice, Knot)
3. HISTORICAL BUG: The 2026-07-29 incident suggests Resolve WAS active then, or workers were running old code
4. ACCUMULATION PATTERN: 115 processes over 11-13h (elapsed 41735-48134s) suggests processes hung and never reaped - possibly wait_with_output() hung at resolve.rs:342-347

Fix required: Add .current_dir(workspace) to Command::new("claude") in resolve.rs:333. Consider adding Resolve to active waterfall OR deprecating the strand entirely if not needed.
issue.title: Investigate: ~100+ claude processes leaked at cwd=$HOME for 11-13h, saturated lab to load 300+

issue.close_reason: Implemented set_resource on all four resilient OTLP exporter wrappers (ResilientGrpcSpanExporter, ResilientHttpSpanExporter, ResilientGrpcLogExporter, ResilientHttpLogExporter). Each wrapper now delegates set_resource calls to the inner exporter via Arc::get_mut, with WARN logging if the Arc is not unique. This fixes the root cause where resource attributes (service.name, service.version, service.instance.id, deployment.cluster, needle.worker.pool) were not reaching the collector. Commit 922dd47 pushed to main.
issue.description:
## Evidence

Raw capture of the deployed needle 0.3.1 binary POSTing to /v1/logs (isolated
HOME, throwaway workspace, compression: none, local receiver) contains NO
resource attributes at all. Every string in the 598-byte payload:

  needle | INFO | {"version":"0.3.1","worker_name":"otelprobe"}
  event_type | worker.booting | worker_id | claude-code-glm-4.7-otelprobe
  session_id | de7fb055 | sequence | event_type | init.step.started | duration_ms

No service.name, no service.version, no deployment.cluster, no
needle.worker.pool, none of needle.agent/needle.model/needle.workspace.

Live dashboard (/api/dashboard, 2026-08-16 04:40 UTC) consequently shows
repo=null, semver=null, worker_pool="default" for EVERY worker in the fleet.
environment is the only field that works, and it is the one field NEEDLE does
not supply — the collector upserts deployment.cluster itself.

## Root cause

opentelemetry_sdk 0.31 pushes the Resource down the chain at provider-build time:
  SdkLoggerProvider::build() -> processor.set_resource()  (logs/logger_provider.rs:267)
  BatchLogProcessor::set_resource() -> BatchMessage::SetResource  (logs/batch_log_processor.rs:323)
  batch worker -> exporter.set_resource()

LogExporter::set_resource (logs/export.rs:153) and SpanExporter::set_resource
(trace/export.rs:74) are DEFAULTED NO-OPS on the SDK traits. src/telemetry/otlp.rs
interposes four wrappers that implement export() and nothing else:

  ResilientHttpLogExporter   (otlp.rs:306)
  ResilientGrpcLogExporter   (otlp.rs:249)
  ResilientHttpSpanExporter  (otlp.rs:192)
  ResilientGrpcSpanExporter  (otlp.rs:135)

Each inherits the no-op, absorbs the Resource, and never forwards it to the
inner opentelemetry_otlp exporter, which then serializes with its default empty
Resource. OtlpSink::build_resource() (otlp.rs:719) is correct — its output is
discarded one hop before the socket.

Metrics are unaffected: MetricExporter is passed to PeriodicReader unwrapped.
That asymmetry is why the collector transform/metric_dimensions rule, which
reads resource.attributes[...], was written against a resource that exists.

Traces to Tempo have the same defect: every NEEDLE span currently arrives with
an empty Resource.

## Deliverables

- Implement set_resource on all four wrappers, delegating to the inner exporter.
  The wrappers hold inner: Arc<...>; the SDK calls set_resource at
  provider-build time while the Arc is still unique, so Arc::get_mut is the
  delegation mechanism. WARN (do not silently continue) if the unique reference
  cannot be obtained.
- Adopt the rule in code review: a wrapper interposed on an OTel SDK exporter
  trait must implement EVERY method of that trait, including defaulted no-ops.

## Acceptance

issue.description:
Implements ADR-005 in docs/adr/ (005-unify...) referenced from plan.md Phase 9.

Today perform_upgrade() (src/upgrade/mod.rs) downloads a new GitHub release and overwrites
env::current_exe() directly, with zero canary validation and zero fleet propagation. Separately,
check_auto_canary()/check_hot_reload() in src/worker/mod.rs already implement a full, tested,
canary-gated hot-reload pipeline that runs every worker-loop cycle -- but it only ever reacts to
a needle-testing binary written by the (disabled) self-modification pipeline. Nothing connects
"new GitHub release" to that channel. Live-confirmed drift during 2026-07-20 audit: ex44's
installed needle reported 0.2.11 while GitHub's latest release was v0.2.12, published the same day.

Deliverables:
1. New function alongside check_for_update() (src/upgrade/mod.rs) that downloads a newer release
   to needle_home/bin/needle-testing instead of overwriting the running binary. Skip (log why) if
   a :testing binary is already present and unpromoted, so this can't clobber an in-flight
   self-modification candidate.
2. Periodic poll in needle supervise (src/supervisor/mod.rs) calling that function on interval
   supervisor.update_check_interval_secs (default 21600), gated behind new
   supervisor.auto_upgrade_check: bool (default false).
3. No changes needed to check_auto_canary()/check_hot_reload() -- verify via test that a
   release-sourced :testing binary is picked up identically to a self-modification-sourced one.
4. Regression tests per plan.md Phase 9.4.

Acceptance criteria: with auto_upgrade_check=true and a mocked newer release, a full poll cycle
produces a promoted :stable and a subsequent hot-reload in worker-loop tests; a failing canary
leaves :stable untouched; needle upgrade (manual path) is unchanged.
issue.title: Wire GitHub-release upgrade path into canary-gated :testing channel (ADR-005)

issue.description:
## Problem

When agent.routing.rules is configured but no rule matches the active model, NEEDLE silently falls back to agent.default (or routing.default_adapter if set). This means a misconfigured or unrecognized model (e.g. a new provider, a typo, a model removed from the adapter list) routes silently to the wrong adapter with no signal to the operator.

## What to add

Add an optional boolean agent.routing.strict (default: false):

  agent:
    routing:
      strict: true
      rules:
        - match_model: "(claude-)?(sonnet|opus|fable|haiku).*"
          adapter: claude-print
        - match_model: "glm.*"
          adapter: claude-code-glm-4.7

When strict: true and no rule matches the active model:
1. Do NOT fall back to agent.default or routing.default_adapter.
2. Emit a RoutingFailed telemetry event with the model name and rule count.
3. Return Err from apply_routing_rules with a clear human-readable message:
   "no routing rule matched model 'gpt-4o' — add a rule to agent.routing.rules or set routing.strict: false to fall back to the default adapter"
4. Propagates through resolve_adapter -> dispatch -> marks the bead as failed (not orphaned), surfaced in the bead list.

## Schema changes

pub struct RoutingConfig {
    pub rules: Vec<RoutingRule>,
    pub default_adapter: Option<String>,
    pub strict: bool,  // new, default false
}

Add RoutingFailed to EventKind:
RoutingFailed {
    bead_id: BeadId,
    model: String,
    rules_tried: usize,
}

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] RoutingConfig has strict: bool (default false); existing configs without strict behave unchanged.
- [ ] strict: true + no match: apply_routing_rules returns Err with the message above; RoutingFailed telemetry emitted.
- [ ] strict: false + no match: existing fallback behavior unchanged.
- [ ] Bead is marked failed (dispatch error), not orphaned or silently retried.
- [ ] Unit tests: strict=true no-match -> Err; strict=false no-match -> default; strict=true match -> Ok.
- [ ] cargo test passes (push and wait for needle-ci).
issue.title: routing: strict mode — fail loudly when no rule matches an unrecognized model

issue.description:
needle status's process-table scan for "unregistered needle run processes" produces massive false-positive counts (93 on ex44, 29 on lab, confirmed 2026-08-13) that do not correspond to real unregistered workers.

Root cause (verified via ps/proc inspection of the flagged PIDs):

1. Child processes of ALREADY-REGISTERED workers get swept in as if they were separate top-level workers. Each registered worker's per-bead pipeline (`bash -c cd <repo> && git rev-parse HEAD > .needle/... `, `claude --print --verbose ...`, `cat`, the `needle-transform-claude` output-piping helper) contains the substring "needle" somewhere in its cmdline (a `.needle/` path or the `needle-transform-claude` binary name), which appears to be enough to match the scanner's heuristic. These are not independent workers — they're already accounted for under their parent's registered identifier.

2. Some flagged PIDs have NO relation to needle at all — orphaned pytest runs, shell scripts (e.g. poll-oauth-usage.sh), an idle `uv run uvicorn` server, stray `sleep` calls, all reparented to PID 1. These appear to be swept in by the scanner walking orphaned (PPID=1) process trees generally, not by any needle-specific match.

Verified by cross-checking against a strict argv match for actual `needle run` invocations (`/needle run --workspace ...`) — that count matches the registered-worker count exactly (12 on ex44, 6 on lab), confirming the fleet itself is healthy and the discrepancy is entirely in the status detector.

Fix should make the "discovered worker" process-table scan match only genuine `needle run` invocations (argv0 resolves to the needle binary AND argv1 == "run"), not any process whose cmdline merely contains the substring "needle", and should not treat arbitrary orphaned process trees as worker candidates.
issue.title: needle status: unregistered-worker scan false-positives on any process with 'needle' in cmdline

ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED AND FIXED. build_http_providers() in src/telemetry/otlp.rs called .with_endpoint(config.endpoint.clone()) for all three OTLP HTTP exporters (traces/metrics/logs), passing the bare configured endpoint with no per-signal path. opentelemetry-otlp only auto-appends /v1/traces, /v1/metrics, /v1/logs when resolving from an OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*_ENDPOINT env var - NOT when .with_endpoint() is called programmatically, which is what NEEDLE does. Every HTTP export request has therefore always hit the collector's bare root (e.g. http://needle-otel-ex44-.../4318/) and gotten a 404, silently and permanently, for every worker that has ever run with otlp_sink.enabled=true.

Confirmed by first fixing the swallowed-error bug (the "sink flush failed: failed to flush logger provider" log line only showed Display, not the wrapped cause - fixed to show the full anyhow chain), then reproducing: the real error was reqwest::Error { kind: Status(404, None), url: ".../4318/" }. Cross-checked directly against the opentelemetry-otlp 0.31.1 crate source (vendored locally) - confirmed with_endpoint() is used verbatim with no path appended, matching the crate's own test suite behavior.

Fix (commit 40de7e3): append the correct /v1/{signal} suffix per exporter before calling with_endpoint(), trimming a trailing slash on the base endpoint first. build_grpc_providers is unaffected (gRPC has no per-signal URL paths).

Live-verified with a scoped diagnostic worker (identifier=otel-fixcheck, local debug build, workspace NEEDLE): boots clean, claims a real bead (bf-47ab9), and its full event stream (worker.booting, bead.claim.attempted/succeeded, build.heartbeat, agent.routing_decision, agent.dispatched, transform.started, worker.state_transition, rate_limit.allowed, init.step.*) is now visible on dashboard.ardenone.com/needle via direct API query - the first real (non-synthetic) worker telemetry this pipeline has ever successfully delivered end-to-end.

Also fixed in the same investigation: a fresh, unrelated compile break on main (bf-5stm4, TimeoutReason missing Display) that was blocking any local build.
issue.description:
## Problem

Confirmed live on ex44 2026-08-12: real fleet workers (rota-1, hoop-1) converted to telemetry.otlp_sink.enabled=true both boot clean (bf-3s2b0/192a2ab's crash fix holds) and hit exactly ONE "NEEDLE telemetry: sink flush failed: failed to flush logger provider" line right as the worker loop starts. That single line is the LAST OTLP-related log line either process ever produces.

Over the following ~5 minutes, both workers stayed completely healthy doing real work (heartbeat files updating every ~30s, rota-1 on bf-576h8, hoop-1 moved from bf-1sy9t to bf-qt5hn - i.e. actually completing/cycling beads), proving the worker/local file_sink telemetry path is unaffected. But queried needle-dashboard's /api/dashboard directly (via a scoped port-forward, bypassing the OAuth gate) 8 times over 160s: zero events, zero worker entries for rota-1 or hoop-1 ever appeared. active_workers stayed 0 the whole time.

By contrast, a separate synthetic curl POST straight to the collector's /v1/logs endpoint (with valid authentication) DID land and IS visible on the dashboard (worker_id=unknown, event_type=test.smoke, timestamped 06:14:04Z) - so the collector, VictoriaLogs, and dashboard side of the pipe are all confirmed working. The break is specifically in NEEDLE's own OTLP exporter: after the first flush failure, it appears to stop trying entirely rather than retrying on the next periodic flush (metrics_interval_secs=10 in this config - there should have been ~30 more flush attempts in that window if the exporter were still alive).

## Hypothesis (not confirmed - nobody has read the actual underlying error)

The "sink flush failed: failed to flush logger provider" message wraps whatever the real reqwest/tonic/opentelemetry-sdk error was, but that inner error is not logged - only the wrapper text is. Two candidate mechanisms:
1. The periodic export task (likely spawned via the same tokio::spawn pattern bf-3s2b0 just fixed for the drop-monitor task) panics or returns early on its first failure and is never restarted - a sibling bug to the one bf-3s2b0 fixed, same file/area (src/telemetry/otlp.rs), different task.
2. The BatchLogProcessor's background worker thread/task exits after an unhandled error from its export attempt, which is normal-ish behavior for some OTel SDK batch processors on certain error classes, but would mean NEEDLE needs its own retry/restart wrapper around it - the SDK default is not to silently resume.

## What to check

- Read the actual error via a debug build or by adding a Display of the underlying error to the "sink flush failed" log line (currently just "failed to flush logger provider" with no source/cause chain rendered).
- Check whether the OTLP log-export background task/thread is still alive after the first failure (thread list, tokio task count, or an explicit liveness marker).
- Check whether this is a race specific to worker startup (first flush landing before something else - e.g. the collector's receiver - is fully warmed up) vs a persistent per-connection failure (e.g. HTTP/2 connection pool issue, DNS caching a bad result once).
- Reproduce with RUST_LOG=debug or equivalent to get more detail than the current single-line warning.

## Acceptance criteria

- Root cause of the first flush failure identified (actual error text captured, not just the wrapper message).
- Fix confirmed: a worker with otlp_sink.enabled=true runs for 5+ minutes, its heartbeat/claim/dispatch events are visible on needle-dashboard's /api/dashboard without needing a synthetic/manual event to prove the pipe works.
- If the fix is "retry on transient export failure", add a regression test forcing one export failure and asserting the exporter keeps trying on subsequent flushes rather than going permanently silent.

## Context

Found while live-verifying bf-3s2b0/192a2ab (the OTLP startup-crash fix) against real fleet workers per user request. That fix is solid - crash is gone - but this is a second, distinct bug in the same area that was masked by the crash bug (nobody could get a worker to stay alive long enough with OTLP on to notice this one until now).
issue.title: OTLP export silently dies after first transient flush failure, never recovers

[migrated comment from bf-2fbz7, 2026-08-11T15:19:25.944217154Z, author cli]
Found 2026-08-11 during a lab incident investigation: bead bf-5vfu in the domain-check repo ("Investigate br claim exclusion logic") accumulated 973,589 events in its events list — almost entirely repeating claimed/assignee_changed pairs from a claim-race/retry loop. This inflated that single bead's JSON record to 246MB (out of a 352-bead, 247MB total .beads/issues.jsonl). The bloated file was committed 153 times, growing domain-check's .git to 4.1GB, and is a strong suspect in a series of git-process OOM kills on lab (7x, 07:32-07:55 EDT, each ~12-13GB RSS) that ultimately took the whole NEEDLE tmux fleet down.

Root gap: NEEDLE/bf never caps or prunes the per-bead events list, so any bead caught in a claim-race loop becomes a ticking git-bloat time bomb once its bead store gets committed. Checked 'bf --help' end to end — no compact/vacuum/prune-events command exists to fix this after the fact either. The 'compaction_level' field on the bead schema suggests this was anticipated but never implemented/wired up.

Could not fix bf-5vfu itself: trimming it would mean hand-editing .beads/issues.jsonl directly, which is a hard prohibition in this environment (must go through bf, never edit .beads/ by hand), and there is no bf command that does it instead.

Suggested fixes: (1) cap events-per-bead in bf/br (e.g. hard limit + oldest-N-dropped or summarized), (2) surface a bf command to compact/truncate a bead's event history, (3) NEEDLE-side: detect and circuit-break a claim-race loop before it can generate hundreds of thousands of events on one bead.
issue.title: Unbounded per-bead events list causes runaway git bloat (no compaction tool)

## Problem

Every adapter already declares which inference provider it uses --
`AgentAdapter.provider: Option<String>` (dispatch/mod.rs:264-266), e.g.
`Some("anthropic")` for builtin_claude_sonnet/builtin_claude_opus,
`Some("openai")` for builtin_codex (dispatch/mod.rd:450,477), `None` for
builtin_opencode. It already backs `AgentAdapter::gen_ai_system()`
(dispatch/mod.rd:320-322, defaults to "local") and rate-limit provider
checks, and already flows into telemetry event *data* for
RateLimitWait/RateLimitAllowed/MendRateLimitCleaned
(telemetry/mod.rs:1493-1498,1503-1505,1764-1775, sourced from
adapter.provider.clone() at dispatch/mod.rs:1652).

It is NOT currently added as an OTLP resource or record attribute anywhere
in otlp.rs, so the value that answers "which company is providing
inference for this worker" -- e.g. for the dashboard.ardenone.com/needle/
worker cards -- cannot be shown. This was raised as UI feedback on that
dashboard 2026-08-16 ("Add another attribute: model provider. It's the
company that's providing the inference.").

## Request

Add `needle.model.provider` following the same dual-layer pattern
ADR-016 established for needle.agent/needle.model (decision table,
"Identity that changes belongs on the record, not the Resource"):
provider can change per-dispatch whenever agent.routing selects a
different adapter, same as model/agent, so:

- Resource layer: the configured default adapter's provider, set in
  OtlpSink::build_resource() alongside the existing needle.agent/
  needle.model resource attributes.
- Record layer: the actually-dispatched adapter's provider, added
  wherever needle-5d246a6d ends up wiring per-record agent/model
  attributes into emit_log -- this bead's work should land alongside
  or after that one rather than inventing a second per-record
  mechanism. Check needle-5d246a6d's status/assignee before starting
  in case the two are worth doing as one change.

## Acceptance criteria

- A worker's OTLP log records (verified via a wire capture, per ADR-016
  Decision #5 -- assert on exported records, not on build_resource()'s
  return value) carry `needle.model.provider` with the adapter's
  declared provider string ("anthropic", "openai", etc.), or are absent
  when the adapter declares no provider (None) -- do not emit an empty
  string or a fabricated default.
- Covers both the boot-time default adapter and, once routing switches
  adapters mid-session, the actually-dispatched adapter's provider.

## Out of scope

This bead only covers NEEDLE-side emission. The dashboard's ingestion
(`normalize_otlp_log`/`public_event`/`get_dashboard_summary` in
declarative-config's needle-dashboard ConfigMap), its data contract doc
(dashboard-site/docs/notes/needle-data-contract.md), and the frontend
worker card do not yet have a provider field at all -- that consumption
work is a separate follow-up once this is emitting.
issue.title: Emit adapter provider (needle.model.provider) as an OTLP attribute

issue.description:
## Symptom

A single worker's stderr log grew to 33.7 GB and was still growing at ~159 GB/hr
when killed. On lab (2026-08-05) this consumed 33 GB of a 444 GB disk in under
30 minutes and was ~50 minutes from filling the root filesystem.

Observed on worker `claude-print-opus-alpha`, workspace `cgov-polish-queue`,
needle 0.2.15.

## Evidence

Each log line carries its full tracing span stack, and the stack never unwinds:

    worker.session{...}:bead.claim{...}:bead.lifecycle{...}:bead.claim{...}:bead.lifecycle{...}...

Measured within one session, same event type:

| sample | bead.claim depth | bead.lifecycle depth | longest line |
|--------|------------------|----------------------|--------------|
| early  | 18               | 18                   | 4,983 bytes  |
| late   | 2,488            | 2,488                | 629,829 bytes |

The two depths are exactly equal, and grow by one pair per claim cycle. Because
every subsequent event re-serializes the whole accumulated stack, total output
grows quadratically — which is why the rate was unremarkable at first and
reached 159 GB/hr about 20 minutes in.

## Root cause

`src/worker/mod.rs:1608`

    self.bead_lifecycle_span = Some(lifecycle_span.entered());

`EnteredSpan` is a RAII guard over the thread-local span stack, which requires
LIFO drop order. On the next claim this line evaluates in the wrong order:

1. `lifecycle_span.entered()` pushes the NEW span onto the stack
2. the assignment then drops the OLD `EnteredSpan`, popping it

The old guard is no longer on top when it drops, so the exit is out of order and
the previous span is never removed. One `bead.lifecycle` leaks per claim cycle.

The same defect hits `bead.claim` at `src/worker/mod.rs:1552`:

    let _claim_enter = claim_span.enter();

`_claim_enter` is dropped at end of scope, i.e. AFTER line 1608 has already
pushed the lifecycle span on top of it — again out of order. This is why
`bead.claim` and `bead.lifecycle` accumulate at identical depth.

The comment at `src/worker/mod.rs:1610` asserts the claim span "is dropped here",
which is not what the code does.

## Deliverables

- Fix the guard ordering so each claim cycle exits its spans LIFO. Options:
  explicitly drop the previous `bead_lifecycle_span` before entering the new one;
  drop `_claim_enter` before line 1608; or stop holding `EnteredSpan` across
  await points / in struct fields and use `Span` + `.in_scope()` / `Instrument`.
- Note: holding an `EnteredSpan` across an `.await` (line 1560) is itself unsound
  for async and is worth removing regardless.
- Add a bound / guard so a runaway span stack can never again produce
  multi-hundred-KB log lines.

## Acceptance criteria

- A worker running >=200 consecutive claim cycles shows constant span depth in
  stderr — not monotonically increasing.
- Regression test asserts span depth after N claims is O(1), not O(N).
- Max observed log line length stays bounded across a long run.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt` clean.

## Repro / artifacts

Samples preserved on lab at `.needle/logs/samples/alpha-stderr-{head,tail}-2MB.log`
(relative to the coding user's home). The head sample shows depth 18, the tail
sample depth 2,488, same session `d5813a0d`.
issue.notes:

[migrated comment from bf-3uj6i, 2026-08-05T20:33:26.472209206Z, author cli]
ROOT CAUSE CORRECTION (verified against tracing-subscriber 0.3.23 source). The stated mechanism -- non-LIFO exit leaving the previous span un-popped -- does not hold. SpanStack::pop does a reverse search and stack.remove(idx), so it removes the span from anywhere in the stack, not just the top; an out-of-order exit on a single thread is harmless. The mechanism that actually leaks is the one noted only in passing at the end of the bead: holding the EnteredSpan across .await. On a multi-thread runtime the task resumes on another thread, the guard drops there, that stack has no matching id, pop() returns false, and the original thread's entry is orphaned. Fixed in c2d83c3 by switching to .instrument(). Note for auditing other enter() call sites: the rule is 'never hold a guard across await', not 'preserve LIFO order'.

issue.description:
Found during the ADR-002 field-guide independent review (2026-08-12). Related to but distinct from the update --status closed defect - this is the reason that defect propagates through a restore instead of being caught at the boundary.

Issue::validate() enforces the invariant that closed issues carry both closed_at and close_reason (src/model.rs:293-302). The two validate() call sites at src/service/checkpoint.rs:2372 and :2584 are on the LEGACY issue-only staging path. The forensic stage path - the one the current flush/restore actually uses - never calls it.

Consequence: an issue with base_status closed and NULL closed_at and NULL close_reason is exported by flush, accepted by sync import-only --restore-into-empty without error, and lands in a fresh workspace as a permanently invalid record. bead doctor also reports schema_validity OK for it.

Fix: call Issue::validate() on the forensic import path and fail the import with a per-record diagnostic. A restore is the last point where an invalid record can be rejected before it becomes indistinguishable from legitimate history.

issue.description:
Found 2026-08-02 during the v0.2.16 release.

bead_store::tests::bf_cli_bead_store_list_all_passes_explicit_limit fails
intermittently in a full 'cargo test --lib' run:

  panicked at src/bead_store/mod.rs:2707:
  called Result::unwrap() on an Err value:
  Os { code: 2, kind: NotFound } -- reading back bf-list-args.txt

The test writes a fake 'bf' shell script into a tempdir, chmods it 0755, calls
list_all(), then reads the args file the script should have written. When it
fails, that file does not exist, i.e. the fake script never ran or never
completed its write.

Passes 3/3 in isolation and passed a second full-suite run (1704/0), so it is
load-dependent, not deterministic. Observed failing in one full local run and
suspected as the third failure in CI workflow needle-ci-manual-x9r67 (which
reported 3 failures where an isolated local run reproduced only 2).

Fix direction: the test already notes it uses a test-specific args file 'to
avoid race conditions', so the remaining race is likely exec-vs-write of the
script itself under load. Consider fsync/close-before-exec, or asserting on
list_all()'s Result instead of ignoring it with 'let _' so the real error
surfaces instead of a downstream NotFound.
issue.notes:
[migrated comment from bf-2mp0y, 2026-08-06T11:13:50.421896128Z, author cli]
Root-caused 2026-08-06: this is a wall-clock timing bug, not a logic bug. Evidence: passes 1711/1711 in a full local --lib run on ex44 (692.81s at a 2-core cap) and passes in 0.00s in isolation; fails only on iad-ci, which takes 1311-1542s for the same suite at a 3-core limit -- about 2x the wall clock for 50 percent more CPU. It failed both runs on 2026-08-06 (needle-ci-x2wx2, needle-ci-vnmhd), blocking every release. The test also hides its own cause: "let _ = store.list_all().await;" discards the real error, so the failure surfaces as an unrelated NotFound panic on the args file -- changing that to .expect() is the fastest way to learn which shared-state interaction loses the race. Raised P3 to P1 because it blocks all releases. Real fix tracked as bf-4icmm (virtual time), which now blocks this bead; see also bf-hu2ag (per-test HOME isolation), since the suite writes into the live fleet state dir.

[migrated comment from bf-2mp0y, 2026-08-06T17:14:06.059833911Z, author cli]
MEASURED FLAKE RATE 2026-08-06: 4 failures in 7 CI runs (57%). All four are this identical test, and all four panic at the same line -- src/bead_store/mod.rs:2736:56, which is "let args = std::fs::read_to_string(&args_file).unwrap();". Failed: needle-ci-x2wx2, needle-ci-vnmhd, needle-ci-f46kr, needle-ci-verify-xjbbm. Passed: needle-ci-8x2jj, needle-ci-kz4qz, needle-ci-xt8tz. Test-suite runtime on the runs that completed: 1243s-1540s. This confirms the earlier diagnosis exactly: the panic is on the args-file read, not on any assertion, because "let _ = store.list_all().await;" one line earlier discarded the real error. It also confirms it is nondeterministic rather than a hard break -- the same commit both passes and fails. At a 57% failure rate this is not an occasional annoyance; it is the dominant reason NEEDLE releases do not ship. Fix is bf-4icmm (virtual time), which blocks this bead.

[migrated comment from bf-2mp0y, 2026-08-07T03:38:20.840183104Z, author cli]
ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-08-07 — and it is NOT the wall-clock timing theory recorded above. That theory was wrong. The real error is ETXTBSY (Text file busy, os error 26) on subprocess spawn: the test writes a fake bf script, chmods it, and execs it while a concurrent fork holds an inherited write fd. Reproduced 15 times in 40 runs (37.5 percent) with "cargo test --lib bead_store::tests -- --test-threads=32". Full analysis in bf-37hoj; fix in bf-2um4a, which now blocks this bead instead of bf-4icmm. Virtual time would not have fixed this.
issue.title: bf_cli_bead_store_list_all_passes_explicit_limit is flaky under parallel load

issue.description:
Fix for bf-37hoj (ETXTBSY on subprocess spawn). Two parts; part 1 alone
resolves the CI flake, part 2 prevents the next one from being misdiagnosed.

PART 1 — treat ETXTBSY as transient on every spawn path (the actual fix)

spawn_version_check (~line 68 of src/bead_store/mod.rs) already does this
correctly and its doc comment already describes the race. Generalise that
handling; do not invent a new pattern.

  Err(e) if e.raw_os_error() == Some(26) && attempt + 1 < MAX_ATTEMPTS => {
      tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20)).await;
  }

Apply at all four unprotected spawn sites:
  - run_br_in    (~line 567, spawn at ~579)
  - run_bf_batch (~line 850, spawn at ~864)
  - run_bf_claim (~line 887, spawn at ~926)
  - run_bf_in    (~line 1591, spawn at ~1608)

run_bf_in and run_br_in already own a retry loop for transient lock errors, but
the spawn is outside it — cmd.spawn()...? returns immediately. Route the spawn
error into that existing loop rather than bolting on a second one: ETXTBSY is
transient in exactly the same sense a lock error is. Keep the existing behaviour
that genuinely non-transient spawn errors (ENOENT, EACCES) still fail fast and
are NOT retried — retrying a missing binary five times only slows the failure.

This is a production fix, not just a test fix. NEEDLE hot-reloads its own binary
and upgrades bf in place, so a worker spawning bf or needle mid-rewrite hits the
same errno and currently fails the whole operation.

PART 2 — stop discarding the error that explains the failure

Four tests do "let _ = store.<call>().await;" one line before asserting on a
file that call was supposed to produce (~lines 2458, 2506, 2559, 2733). Because
workspace and args_file are the same tempdir, the discarded error and the panic
have the same underlying cause, but only the misleading one is reported. Replace
each with .expect("..."), so any future spawn failure names itself instead of
surfacing as an unrelated NotFound.

The two exclude_ids tests (panics at ~2604 and ~2667) follow the same shape and
should get the same treatment.

ACCEPTANCE
  - cargo test --lib bead_store::tests -- --test-threads=32, run 40 times,
    produces 0 failures. Baseline before the fix was 15/40 (37.5 percent).
  - No test in this file discards a Result whose failure it then asserts on.
  - A deliberately missing binary still fails immediately, not after 5 retries.

DO NOT bother converting these tests to tokio virtual time (bf-4icmm). That was
based on the earlier wall-clock theory, which bf-37hoj disproves — the failure
is an exec race, not a timeout, and virtual time would not have fixed it.
issue.title: Retry ETXTBSY on every bead_store spawn path, and stop discarding spawn errors in tests

Where a run's time goes today:
- apt-get + rustup + gh apt repo install: every run, from a bare debian:bookworm

Child beads cover: dependency lockfile, prebuilt builder image, sccache, split
verify/release stages, retry-strategy fix, and the test-suite changes that are
the actual bulk of the runtime.

Two workflow-template children live in the declarative-config repo, not here:
k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/needle-workflowtemplate.yml. Those go through ArgoCD
(edit manifest, commit, push, let it sync) -- never kubectl apply.

- `check-version-change`: 500m CPU / 1Gi memory (limits: 1000m / 2Gi)
- `release`: 1500m CPU / 4Gi memory (limits: 3000m / 6Gi)

- PriorityClass: None (uses default cluster priority)
- Node selector: None
- Affinity: None

**Image:** `ronaldraygun/needle-ci-builder:0.1.5-with-deps`

### iad-ci Cluster Node Eligibility
Source: `kubectl get nodes` + `kubectl top nodes` (iad-ci)

**Node pool composition:**
- 3x small nodes (`compute1-4`): 2 cores capacity, 1.5 allocatable cores, ~3.8Gi memory
- 3x large nodes (`compute1-8`): 4 cores capacity, 3.5 allocatable cores, ~7.6Gi memory

**Actual usage (top nodes):**
- Small nodes: 11-35% CPU, 78-87% memory — **memory-constrained**
- Large nodes: 9-19% CPU, 19% memory — **substantial headroom**

All nodes eligible for needle-ci (no taints or selectors restricting placement).

### Resident Workloads (Requested Resources)
Source: `kubectl get pods -n argo-workflows` (Running phase only)

**Per-node resident requests (allocatable subtracted):**
- `adb-relay`: 10m+10m CPU / 32Mi+16Mi memory (2 containers)
- `argo-workflows-iad-ci-server`: 50m CPU / 128Mi memory
- `argo-workflows-iad-ci-workflow-controller`: 100m CPU / 128Mi memory
- `coned-bootstrap`: 25m CPU / 64Mi memory

Total resident: <200m CPU / <400Mi memory per large node.

### Calculated Headroom (Large Nodes)

- CPU: 3500m
- Memory: ~6.3Gi

- CPU: 3300m (3.3 cores)

issue.description: GitHub issue #11 (jarvis-laboratories). Supervisor::spawn_worker (src/supervisor/mod.rs) builds its child via Command::new("needle"), a bare $PATH lookup. issue.close_reason: Fixed help text accuracy: stop --all now warns supervisors may survive and requires manual pgrep verification; supervise --workspace now clarifies it monitors that workspace exclusively without auto-discovery
issue.description:
Companion to bf-4iwog (which covers `needle run --workspace`). This bead covers
the remaining help-text accuracy gaps, with `stop` as the serious one.

1. `needle stop --all` — CURRENTLY WRONG, and it matters

   Help says:   --all    Stop all needle workers

   Observed 2026-08-07 stopping a 17-worker fleet: `needle stop --all` killed the
   tmux sessions (the tmux server itself went away) but every supervisor survived,
   reparented to init:

     pid=1287492 state=S ppid=1 elapsed=05:31 children=2 --identifier alpha
     ... 8 identical

   They then ignored SIGINT entirely — both the supervisors and their children —
   while stuck in the pre-dispatch shell. Only SIGKILL cleared them. The command
   also printed its own contradiction:

     "kill attempt reported success but 3 process(es) still running"

   An operator reading the help concludes the fleet is stopped. It is not: the
   supervisors keep running, keep their claims, and can keep dispatching. This is
   the difference between "the fleet is down" and "the fleet looks down", and it
   is exactly the state you must NOT be in before rewriting git history or doing
   anything else that assumes quiescence.

   Suggested wording:

     --all
         Kill the tmux session of every registered worker.
         This does NOT reliably terminate the worker supervisors: a
         `needle run` process whose session is killed is commonly reparented
         to init and keeps running, and may ignore SIGINT. After this
         command, verify with `pgrep -af needle-stable run` and signal any
         survivors directly. See `needle cleanup` for session hygiene.

2. `needle supervise --workspace` — same ambiguity as bf-4iwog

   Help says:  Workspace to monitor (defaults to config workspace)
   Unclear whether the supervisor scales workers for that one workspace only, or
   uses it as a home while auto-discovery applies. Should state which.

3. `needle cleanup` is the model to copy — no change needed

   Its help already spells out exactly what the destructive flag does and when to
   use the safe form. The other subcommands should match that standard. Worth
   noting so nobody "fixes" it.

Acceptance: `needle stop --help` states that supervisors may survive and tells
the operator how to verify; `needle supervise --help` disambiguates scope.

NOTE: filed rather than hand-edited because a worker was EXECUTING in this repo
at filing time.
issue.title: needle stop --all help claims it stops workers; it only kills tmux sessions and orphans supervisors

issue.close_reason: Created ADR-015 rejecting full per-worktree isolation. Accepted shared working directories as deliberate design constraint, enforced through operational discipline (one worker per repo for build-heavy workspaces) and bead-level serialization (explicit blocking dependencies for overlapping work). Updated plan.md §6.9 to reference the decision; documented rationale in /home/coding/CLAUDE.md.
issue.notes:
[migrated comment from bf-53iu0, 2026-07-30T03:20:44.697578162Z, author cli]
GAP (plan-vs-artifacts): docs/plan/plan.md §6.9 (lines ~4085-4092) is the only flagged open question in the plan that is NOT resolved in code and NOT tracked by any existing bead or ADR.

EVIDENCE
- No per-worker isolation exists in src/: grep for `worktree` across src/ returns nothing. `bead.workspace` is passed through verbatim as the `{workspace}` template var into the dispatched agent process (src/dispatch/mod.rs), so every worker assigned to a repo runs its agent in the SAME working directory.
- The per-workspace claim flock (plan §6.1, ~line 219; src/claim/) guards only the CLAIMING step's `br update --claim`, NOT the EXECUTING phase. Once two workers are each dispatched into the same repo (with DISTINCT beads), their agents can run concurrent `git add`/`commit`/`reset --hard`/`checkout` in one shared tree for the full duration of both dispatches; one agent's `reset --hard`/`checkout` can discard another's uncommitted work.
- §6.6's flock protects only NEEDLE's own post-hoc Bead-Id trailer amend (src/commit_hook.rs), not the agents' concurrent work.
- Distinct from bf-1ne6u (atomic-claim duplicate-dispatch of the SAME bead) — §6.9 is the broader shared-working-directory hazard that persists even when claiming is correct and beads are distinct.
- docs/adr/ contains ADRs 001-010; none covers this. The plan explicitly states it 'should be captured as its own ADR before implementation ... a bigger design decision than the rest of Phase 6.'

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. New ADR under docs/adr/ (Context/Decision/Alternatives/Consequences) deciding between the two directions the plan names: (a) full git-worktree isolation per worker (incl. merge-back strategy + effect on commit_hook trailer injection), or (b) accept as a known constraint + add a needle-run help/docs callout that >1 worker per repo is unsafe unless beads avoid overlapping file/branch state.
2. plan.md §6.9 updated to reference the ADR and record the chosen direction (remove 'not yet decided').
3. If direction (a): follow-up implementation bead filed. If direction (b): the needle run --help / docs callout is added so the constraint is discoverable at point of use.

NOTE: plan Phase 7 (§7.1a cleanup pane_pid regression) and Phase 8 (§8.3 Explore rediscovery staleness) are BOTH already fixed in code (filter_sessions_for_cleanup_impl walks the process tree via find_needle_process_in_tree; ExploreStrand has rediscover_workspaces + rediscovery_cycles). Their plan Status lines are stale doc drift, not a code gap, so no bead was filed for those.
issue.title: Decide + record ADR for concurrent same-repo worker isolation (plan §6.9 shared working directory)
